Job description – 
Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) Coordinator


 


 


Name of the company: Carpenters Agricultural and Manufacturing Ltd, T/A Globe (CAML)


Primary Location: Globe factory, Independence Drive, Madang, and the residential locations around the town


Job Title: Occupational Health & Safety Coordinator


Contract: Full-time. Starting with 3 months’ probation period


Reporting to: Operations Manager


 


Scope
:


The OHS Coordinator is responsible for coordinating, implementing, and monitoring the company’s Occupational Safety and Health (OHS) management system to ensure compliance with applicable legal requirements and internal standards. This role supports the prevention of workplace injuries, illnesses, and incidents through effective safety programs, training, inspections, and continuous improvement initiatives.


Primary responsibilities and operational tasks:




Review and development of the OHS policies and programs


Lead implementation of OH&S management systems and procedures


Implement training and coaching programs and execute them


Promote and facilitate Risk Management Procedures


Conduct daily site inspections to identify issues, non-conformities, and risk factors on operational procedures and PPEs


Ensure all the safety equipment, firefighting equipment, and emergency equipment are serviced and updated


Conduct emergency evacuation drills, identify the risks, and implement the corrective measures


Coordinate with line managers to promote and monitor the implementation of control measures and action items


Conduct regular system audits and workplace inspections against OH&S management standards, systems, and procedures


Carry out the timely and effective notification, reporting, and investigations into incidents to identify the root cause/s.


Liaise with group HR management and government departments to manage the information flow and process control


Oversee all the installations, maintenance, and disposal of substances


Actively demonstrate and promote safe work attitudes and practices


Facilitate monthly OH&S management review meetings and report


Provide specialist support to all the visitors and on-site contractors in the areas of OH&S system compliances


Demonstrate a high level of personal commitment to the “Incident-Free Operations”


The role demands daily on-site monitoring and conducts OH&S management systems




 


Qualification:


 
Tertiary qualification in Occupational Health & Safety or related field


 


Experience:


3-5 years in a similar field

28787.description:
Job Title – Maintenance Seamer Mechanic


Name of the company: Carpenters Agricultural and Manufacturing Ltd, T/A Globe


Primary Business: Food manufacturing and trading


Location: Independence Drive, Madang


Contract: Permanent Position


Reporting to: Seaming Manager


Salary and Benefits - Negotiable


 


Job Scope:


The Maintenance Seamer Mechanic is responsible for maintaining, adjusting, troubleshooting, repairing, and overhauling a variety of can seamers to ensure they operate safely, efficiently, and to quality standards. Key equipment includes Angelus 29V, Goets 12P, Interpack 1.57 and Hema/Interpack Trapezoidal seamers. This role also serves as a Line Mechanic for additional plant equipment, including fillers, conveyors, can washers, sterilizers, and basket loaders/unloaders.


The role involves mechanical, hydraulic, pneumatic, electrical, and steam systems and requires a strong focus on seam integrity and food safety. Duties cover equipment set-up, changeovers, preventive and emergency maintenance, fabrication, installations, and addressing quality and safety issues.


Job functions:




Perform all job duties in a safe and food-safe manner, following GMPs and company safety policies.


Cannery mechanic is responsible for setting up the lines for production


Carryout necessary services and repairs


Troubleshoot problems


24hr on call duty


Adjust and set the seam profiles as per the given standards (double seam profile)


Carryout seam tests


Responsible for all running repairs


Guide seam operators as to fulfill the daily targets


Disassemble and reassemble equipment for sanitation


Communicate key updates to the manager in charge


Work with the Storeman to ensure availability of critical parts; properly sign out all items per maintenance policy and generate part requests as needed.


Ensure all product contact surfaces are protected during work; complete proper cleanup after each task.




 


Requirements & qualifications




Hands-on experience on continuous fillers, clinchers, and round/trapezoidal can seamers


Sound knowledge of machine overhauling and daily maintenance


Candidates who are familiar with Hema, Canco, Goetz, and Angelus machines are preferred


Good knowledge of English


Willing to work long hours


Age between 30-50

Health Extension Officer
. This position is based in

HEALTH EXTENSION OFFICER


Job Purpose:


The Health Assistant/Health Extension Officer will support the health and well-being of employees and their families within New Britain Palm Oil Limited's – WNB operations, ensuring adherence to health protocols and providing primary healthcare services.


Main Responsibilities:




Provide basic medical care, first aid, and emergency responses to employees and their dependents.

Manage and maintain medical supplies and equipment.

Diploma or Bachelor Degree in Health Science (Rural Health).


Current and valid registration/license with PNG Medical Board.


5 years or more of experience in a clinical or community health setting, preferably in an industrial or rural environment.


Proficiency in first aid and emergency care.


Strong understanding of occupational health and safety principles.


Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.


Ability to work independently and as part of a team.


Proficient in record-keeping and basic computer skills.

28637.description:
Lecturer


School of Business & Management (SoBM) - Port Moresby, NCD




 












Position:
 Lecturer


Department:
 School of Business Management 


Reports to:
 Academic Coordinator


Location:
 IBS College of TVET


Employment Type:
 Full-Time


 


Position Overview:


The Lecturer in Business Management plays a pivotal role in delivering quality education and fostering the academic development of students in business-related disciplines. This position involves assisting with teaching, curriculum development, research, and mentoring, contributing to the overall success of the Business Management Course run at IBS College of TVET.


 


Key Responsibilities:


1. Teaching and Learning:




Preparing and delivering lectures, tutorials, and workshops in Business Management and related subjects.


Facilitate interactive learning experiences to engage students and enhance their understanding of core business concepts.


Develop teaching materials, lesson plans, and assessment tools in collaboration with senior lecturers.




2. Curriculum Development:




Support the development and periodic review of the Business Management curriculum to ensure it meets industry and academic standards.


Integrate contemporary business practices, case studies, and trends into teaching content.




3. Student Support:




Provide academic guidance and mentoring to students to help them achieve their learning objectives.


Assess and evaluate students’ performance through assignments, projects, and examinations.




4. Research and Professional Development:




Participate in research activities and encourage student involvement in research projects.


Stay updated with current business trends, practices, and theories to inform teaching methods.




5. Administrative Duties:




Maintain accurate records of student attendance, progress, and assessment outcomes.


Contribute to departmental meetings, committees, and administrative tasks as required.




6. Community Engagement:




Support outreach programs, workshops, and seminars that promote business education.


Engage with local businesses and organizations to create partnerships and learning opportunities.




 


Qualifications and Experience:




Education:



A Bachelor’s degree in Human Resource Management, Business Management, or a related field is essential.


A Master’s degree (or working towards one) in Business Administration or a similar discipline is highly desirable.






Experience:



More than 3 years of teaching or professional experience in business or management roles.


Prior experience in teaching at the tertiary or vocational education level is an advantage.






Technical Skills:



Knowledge of core business functions such as marketing, finance, management, HR management, and entrepreneurship.


Proficiency in using educational technology tools and learning management systems like Moodle and ERP






Soft Skills:



Strong communication and interpersonal skills.


Effective time management and organizational abilities.


A collaborative mindset and enthusiasm for teaching and student success.








 


Key Competencies:




Ability to explain complex business concepts in an accessible and engaging manner.


Commitment to fostering a supportive and inclusive learning environment.


Adaptability to evolving educational methodologies and industry trends.


Analytical and problem-solving skills relevant to business contexts.




 


Benefits and Opportunities:




Opportunities for professional growth and research involvement.


Collaborative and dynamic work environment.


Access to modern teaching resources and tools.




 


Application Process:


Interested candidates are invited to submit their resume, a cover letter, and relevant academic or professional certifications trough the link provided.


 


IBS College of TVET is an equal opportunity employer and is dedicated to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace.











    	        
Apply

With more than 40 years of experience working in PNG, World Vision International Papua New Guinea (WVIPNG) focuses on helping the most vulnerable children and adults experience fullness of life.  Inspired by our Christian faith, WVPNG has an exciting opportunity for someone who may be looking for a change and wants to become part of a dynamic team helping vulnerable people and communities.


World Vision International Papua New Guinea (WVIPNG) has exciting opportunity for those of you who want a change and want to become part of a dynamic team. We are currently looking for suitable, qualified, experienced, and highly motivated professional to fill the role of 
Project Officer - X2 
to be based in 
Mendi , Southern Highlands Province & Daru, Western Province


PURPOSE OF THE POSITION


The purpose of this role is to role will be responsible for the implementation of RISE DRR & Rapid Response interventions at the Area Program ensuring that WV Papua New Guinea actively collaborates with Partners and communities to ensure:


• National Office, inclusive of Area Program Offices, has improved adaptive organisational 
and staff capacities in disaster management that are responsive to the needs of the context 
of Papua New Guinea.


• WVPNG respond effectively to emergencies; including natural disaster and conflicts, for 
dignity and life; and rebuild disaster-affected communities and sustained well being

EDUCATIONAL QUALIFICATION/SKILLS, KNOWLEDGE & EXPERIENCE




Diploma or University degree in social science or science strand


Minimum one years’ experience preferably in an international NGO environment.


Has an extensive knowledge and experience in all areas of Disaster Risk Reduction, Anticipatory Actions, Emergency Response, WaSH, livelihood, conflict and/or Natural Disasters


Technical knowledge and experience in Disaster Risk Reduction, Anticipatory Actions, WaSH & Livelihood.

Good communication and reporting skills

Proven ability to adapt and perform well in high-pressure and dynamic work environments and situations.


Fluency in English is required. Professional working proficiency in Tok Pisin is preferred.

28882.description:
Newmont produces metals the world needs - safely, responsibly and with care for people, communities and the environment. With a 100+ year history, we continue to shape the future of mining through innovation and strong operational performance. By joining our inclusive, world-class team, you can help shape the future of mining and make a meaningful difference.


 


Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.


 


We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.


 








Your Impact






 


As part of the team, you will lead the delivery of mid- to long-term mine plans that align with production targets, strategic objectives, and regulatory requirements. You will play a critical role in optimising mine design, sequencing, and scheduling to maximise resource recovery and operational efficiency. Working closely with geology, engineering, and operations teams, you will ensure integrated and practical planning outcomes, monitor performance against plan, and implement improvements that enhance productivity, reduce costs, and support safe, reliable mining operations.










As part of the team, you will:








Supervise and coordinate mine planning activities to ensure alignment with operational goals


Develop and maintain mid- and long-term mine plans, schedules, and forecasts


Analyse production data, track performance, and address variances


Provide technical guidance and support to the mine planning team


Foster collaboration across geology, engineering, and operations functions


Identify and drive continuous improvement opportunities in planning processes


Manage risk by identifying, assessing, and implementing mitigation strategies


Lead and contribute to a positive, productive, and safety-focused team environment












Prerequisites for the Role








Degree in 
Mining Engineering


Minimum 
5 years’ experience
 in mining operations, preferably in open cut mining


Strong knowledge of mine design, scheduling, and forecasting


Experience with 
MinePlan, Deswik, and Modular Mining systems


Solid understanding of drill & blast and its impact on load and haul


Demonstrated capability in data analysis, performance monitoring, and reporting


Sound knowledge of PNG Mine Safety Act and mining safety systems


Strong leadership, communication, and stakeholder engagement skills


Ability to work effectively in a 
multinational and remote operating environment












Your work environment






 


This role is offered on a 
21:21 days only
 Fly in, Fly out (FIFO) roster to Lihir Island, PNG.
Our FIFO employees stay in a secure and comfortable camp, in an en-suited and airconditioned room equipped with mini fridge, TV and Wi-Fi. A variety of healthy meal options are catered for at our mess; and the wet mess provides a relaxed social setting where employees can unwind with a game of pool or darts.










At Newmont, our people are our strength and we’re committed to a safe, inclusive and supportive workplace. If you’re passionate about doing work that matters, join Newmont and help shape the future of mining.​






Learn more about our purpose and values: 
About Newmont
​
Hear from our people: 
Life at Newmont
​






Important: Newmont does not ask candidates to pay money or share sensitive personal data outside our secure application process. If this happens, please report it to our Business Integrity team: 
[email protected]
.

28858.description:
Job Type:
 
Permanent
 
About us 


K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate. 


We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.


About the role


In this role you will provide management and leadership within our mobile maintenance department. This rewarding role will see you provide daily mentoring, guidance, instruction, and training to the national workforce to increase safety performance, machinery uptime and efficient outcomes within a motivated and talented department.


Key Accountabilities




Give direction, delegate tasks and provide technical assistance to subordinates.


Liaise with senior maintenance leadership on planned maintenance.


Maintain stock levels and place orders as required.


Ensure cost control measures are considered by utilizing resources available to full capacity.


Ensure training requirements are met.


Organise and document weekly safety toolbox meetings workshop safety representatives.


Regularly monitors and evaluates staff performance in consultation with Mobile Maintenance Superintendent.


Provide coaching for performance improvement.


In conjunction with mobile maintenance superintendent, takes disciplinary action to address performance deficiencies, in accordance with the Company’s rules, policies and procedures.


Personally, responds to inquiries and complaints from the employees.


Responds to emergency situations as necessary.


Carry out other relative duties as directed by the Mobile Maintenance Superintendent.


Maintain safety work standards in accordance with government regulations and company policy.


Perform all roles and responsibilities that support and reflect the company’s mission and core values.




About You 


Qualifications & Experience




Relevant trade qualification in Heavy Equipment Fitting, Auto Electrical and Automation. Minimum Certificate III required.


10+ years relevant work experience essential.


Ability to plan, assign, direct and coordinate a variety of functional specialties (areas) with overlapping work areas.


Must have at least 5 years in mobile fleet maintenance in a supervisory capacity. Should also have experience in training of both operating and maintenance personnel.


Experience in the use of Pronto will be advantageous.


Sound planning, analytical and problem-solving skills.


Excellent trouble shooting skills.


Self-motivated with the ability to work under pressure and autonomously.


Excellent attention to detail and time management skills to meet deadlines.


Strong active listening & interpersonal skills for rapport building, conflict resolution & training.


Actively promotes a safe and healthy culture.




Life at K92  


K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.


Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.


At K92, we want all employees to share in our success, so as well as a competitive salary, employees also participate in our long- and short-term incentive plans, we also provide employees with access to savings incentive programs, medical assistance and the option to salary sacrifice for certain expenses.


In addition to all of this, employees can also access our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.


THIS POSITION IS OPEN ONLY TO CANDIDATES WHO HAVE THE RIGHT TO LIVE & WORK IN PNG WITHOUT SPONSORSHIP 





    	        
Apply

28857.description:
With more than 40 years of experience working in PNG, World Vision International Papua New Guinea (WVIPNG) focuses on helping the most vulnerable children and adults experience fullness of life.  Inspired by our Christian faith, WVPNG has an exciting opportunity for someone who may be looking for a change and wants to become part of a dynamic team helping vulnerable people and communities.


World Vision International Papua New Guinea (WVIPNG) has exciting opportunity for those of you who want a change and want to become part of a dynamic team. We are currently looking for suitable, qualified, experienced, and highly motivated professional to fill the role of 
Learning & Development Officer
 
to be based in 
Port Moresby, National Capital District. 


PURPOSE OF THE POSITION


This position plays an important role to the CB & ER section and P&C Department as a whole. L&D Officer, is a credentialed professional who performs Learning and Development and Employee Relations duties at WVPNG. The duties include assisting with Capacity Building activities, Employee Relations, compiling and maintaining records, review policies and other strategic organisational development initiatives which includes coordinating Our Voice Survey, sharing of the OV survey results and tracking OV action items.


MAJOR ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES


CAPACITY BUILDING




Facilitation of P&C Policy information sessions and other P&C workshops as required.


Facilitation of in – house training programs as required.


Scheduling and coordinating of monthly Learning & Reflection at the National Office


Liaising with external training providers for course information and quotations


Assist L&D Coordinator in the administration of capacity building activities like training, talent management, succession planning and career path planning as required.


Assist with sending of training advice to employees nominated to attend trainings--


Maintain and update accurate training record for all staff training activities carried out at WVPNG on spread sheet and smart sheet-- 




STAFF ORIENTATIONS




Coordinate and facilitate new employee’s induction and orientation (face to face or virtual) in accordance with P&C policies and procedure's


Work with the AP leadership to ensure Orientations is run during the monthly Learning & Reflection Week and or during other visits depending on staff availability


Ensure all new staff are orientated within the first 3 months of commencement with WVPNG


Work with the AP leadership to ensure Orientations is run during the monthly Learning & Reflection WVPNG




STAFF ENGAGEMENT




Assist L&D Coordinator provide information to the regional OV team as and when required


Assist with tracking, monitoring and ensuring the Our Voice survey is completed within expected time frame


Schedule sessions with Departments and APs for the sharing of OV Survey results


Facilitate sessions on OV Survey results with departments /APs as required




 
PERFORMANCE MANAGEMENT & OTHERS




Understand the Performance management system (PFP) at WVPNG well and able to provide correct information on PFP to staff and managers


Assist with Partnering for Performance initiatives – Reminding staff and following up with them on the return of completed PFP Forms


Prepare and provide Audit documents as and when required


Lead and support Christian activities that enrich and develop mutual growth in Christ




EMPLOYEE RELATIONS




Provide support and advice to managers/supervisors on process in dealing with poor work performance and performance counselling


Preparation of warning, suspension and termination letters as required in accordance with the WVPNG policy and procedures.


Ensure up to date filing of all Termination, Warning, Suspension letters and PIP in staff personal file


Maintain and update ER tracker around Performance Issues on a regular basis


Provide support and advice to staff/ Managers in implementing performance management and review processes


Ensure confidentiality is maintained at all times when dealing with or having access sensitive P&C information (incl. employee grievances and disciplinary cases).


Assist with or perform other ER tasks assigned by P&C Manager or Director.


Support the P&C Manager/Director to Conduct Investigation based on staff Issues raised




 


EDUCATIONAL QUALIFICATION/SKILLS, KNOWLEDGE & EXPERIENCE




Bachelor’s Degree or equivalent


Minimum of at least 2 to 3 years in areas of Human Resource/ Training/Employee Relation


PNG HR Professional certification


A sound understanding of all areas in Human resource Management and integration of each of this function.


Excellent oral and written English communication skills


Good facilitation and presentation skills


Demonstrated collaboration & team building skills


Competent in the use of Microsoft Office computer programs including Word, Excel, and PowerPoint




A competitive salary, benefits, and career development opportunity will be offered commensurate with relevant experience, knowledge, and qualifications.


Interested applicants should submit the following documents all in one PDF file before;
 Friday 23 October, 2026, (Midnight, PNG Time)




Expression of interest


Detailed CV




World Vision is committed to the principles of workplace diversity. Qualified women and people with disabilities are encouraged to apply.


World Vision is committed to safeguarding all children and adults living where World Vision operates. We enforce a zero tolerance policy for any forms of violence, abuse and exploitation against children or adults, either by employees or others affiliated with our work. We do not employ staff whose background is not aligned with our safe guarding practices. Employment is conditional upon successful completion of all mandatory background checks, including criminal record checks, where required.


We appreciate the time it takes to prepare your application. Please note that only short-listed candidates suitable for interviews will be contacted. If you do not hear from World Vision within 
two (2) weeks
 of the closing date, please consider your application unsuccessful.

28837.description:
With more than 40 years of experience working in PNG, World Vision International Papua New Guinea (WVIPNG) focuses on helping the most vulnerable children and adults experience fullness of life.  Inspired by our Christian faith, WVPNG has an exciting opportunity for someone who may be looking for a change and wants to become part of a dynamic team helping vulnerable people and communities.


World Vision International Papua New Guinea (WVIPNG) has exciting opportunity for those of you who want a change and want to become part of a dynamic team. We are currently looking for suitable, qualified, experienced, and highly motivated professional to fill the role of 
Security & Transport Director
 to be based in 
Port Moresby, National Capital District, Papua New Guinea.
 The position reports to the National Director.


PURPOSE OF THE POSITION


The Security and Transport Director provides national strategic leadership for security, crisis preparedness, transport, fleet and marine safety, and continuity planning across WVPNG. The role is accountable for maintaining fit-for-purpose security systems, developing staff capability, overseeing security-related incident management, and providing timely risk advice to the National Director and SLT. The Security and Transport Director coordinates closely with operational and enabling functions while ensuring that functional ownership for employee relations, enterprise risk, property, workplace safety and financial decisions remains with the authorised responsible functions.


Major Responsibilities




Lead the development and implementation of the WV PNG security strategy, aligned with WVI SSR policy, WVPNG policy, the PNG context and international best practice.






Provide technical advice and support to the National Director on security and crisis management issues and their likely impact on World Vision operations.






Provide management and leadership support to the Field Security Officer, Transport Supervisor, Security Focal Points and drivers, including leading security recruitment.






Develop the capability and succession pipeline of security, fleet and driver staff through development plans, coaching and role-appropriate training.






Work with senior management to ensure security budgets are in alignment with the assessed level of risk.






Maintain and formally review Country Risk Ratings at defined intervals and whenever material changes occur.






Maintain current Security Risk Assessments and security context analyses through defined review cycles and exception-based updates.






Maintain, monitor and report compliance with Core Security Requirements in line with the National Office risk rating.






Provide security and transport risk input to the national risk register and enterprise-risk processes, and ensure significant and fast-moving risks are escalated to leadership on time.






Ensure security incidents are reported in the Integrated Incident Management (IIM) system and managed as per IIM notification protocols.






Conduct or support security-related fact-finding, evidence preservation, after-action reviews and technical analysis for security incidents.






Maintain and apply a documented escalation protocol for critical incidents, serious injury and fatalities, and coordinate security inputs to IMT/CMT responses.






Lead security and transport inputs to crisis-management and business-continuity preparedness, including exercises, after-action reviews and recovery planning.






Ensure lessons learnt from significant incidents are built into the risk management process to reduce repeat incidents.






Ensure transport policies and procedures are reviewed regularly and that the safety of staff in WV vehicles, boats, buses and motorbikes is paramount.






Oversee road, fleet and marine safety controls, including journey management, driver and skipper standards, accident reporting and insurance coordination.






Ensure all transport operations comply with Government regulations and World Vision policies, and that all WVPNG vehicles are well maintained and auditable.






Provide National Office oversight of all marine operations and ensure marine SOPs and policies are current and relevant to PNG.






Develop and implement a security capacity building plan based on the security risk assessment.






Identify and facilitate security training for high-risk environments, including Security Risk Management Training (SRMT) for leadership teams and Security Awareness in National Theatres (SAINT) for local staff.






Manage and train Security Focal Points to deliver Security Context Analysis, Security Risk Assessments and context-specific Acceptance, Protection and Deterrence strategies.






Ensure all drivers complete defensive driving and first aid training, and qualify local staff as Drive Safe and SAINT instructors, including Training of Trainers.






Ensure staff, new staff and visitors receive security briefings and orientation.






Conduct security analysis, map armed actors and develop scenarios to provide ongoing strategic and situational awareness of shifts in the security environment.






Act as the principal link between the National Office and the WV Office of Corporate Security (OCS), liaising with the Regional Security Director on local security issues.






Co-lead the NGO Security Coordination Network, link in with UNDSS, and maintain strong relationships with the UN, development partners, GoPNG authorities and security service providers.


Where relevant, support civil-military-police relations and use HISS-CAM to inform decision-making while balancing humanitarian principles and operational needs.


Provide crisis support to other offices as requested by Regional OCS.




KNOWLEDGE/QUALIFICATIONS FOR THE ROLE




Minimum five years’ relevant experience in security, resilience, business continuity, transport or crisis management in complex, high-risk or fragile operating environments, whether national or international, including demonstrated leadership experience.






Previous experience in the professional security arena (INGO, Corporate, Military, Law Enforcement, or Emergency Services)






Proven ability to transfer knowledge to security and transport team






Experience in liaising with various levels of Government, International Organizations and NGOs






Practical knowledge of tools mechanisms and procedures for Security Risk






Have a broad understanding of the Regional and Global security issues






Relevant bachelor’s degree or equivalent in Security Management, Risk Management, Strategic Studies, International Relations or Emergency Management or other management discipline






Working knowledge of INGO security practices






Direct application of security and risk management framework within complex NGO operating and organizational environments and proven experience in security risk assessments, security planning and crisis management in the humanitarian context






Understanding of implementing Core Security Requirements, Minimum Operating Security Standards or equivalent


Demonstrated ability to influence and deliver effective organizational outcomes related to all aspects of security and risk management


SAINT instructor certification is desirable; where not already held, the successful candidate must be willing and able to obtain it within an agreed period.


HEAT instructor certification is desirable; where not already held, the successful candidate must be willing and able to obtain it within an agreed period.




A competitive salary, benefits, and career development opportunity will be offered commensurate with relevant experience, knowledge, and qualifications.


Interested applicants should submit the following documents all in 
one PDF file
 before;
 Friday 23 October 2026
, 
(Midnight, PNG Time).




Expression of interest


Detailed CV




World Vision is committed to the principles of workplace diversity. Qualified women and people with disabilities are encouraged to apply.


World Vision is committed to safeguarding all children and adults living where World Vision operates. We enforce a zero tolerance policy for any forms of violence, abuse and exploitation against children or adults, either by employees or others affiliated with our work. We do not employ staff whose background is not aligned with our safe guarding practices. Employment is conditional upon successful completion of all mandatory background checks, including criminal record checks, where required.


We appreciate the time it takes to prepare your application. Please note that only short-listed candidates suitable for interviews will be contacted. If you do not hear from World Vision within 
two (2) weeks
 of the closing date, please consider your application unsuccessful.


Applicant Types Accepted:


Local and International Applicants (IA's) Accepted





    	        
Apply

28810.description:
Don’t come for an easy career. Stay for a rewarding one.
 


Santos is a global energy company committed to increasingly cleaner energy and fuels production, with operations across Australia, Papua New Guinea, Timor-Leste and North America.  


We are currently PNG’s largest single investor and most active explorer, operating all the country’s producing oil fields and holding an extensive appraisal and exploration portfolio. Our aspirations and strategies reflect our genuine commitment to making a meaningful contribution to the lives of Papua New Guineans.


At Santos, our commitment is to be a global leader in the transition to cleaner energy and clean fuels, by helping the world decarbonise to reach net-zero emissions in an affordable and sustainable way.  


Santos is one of Australia’s biggest domestic gas supplier, a leading Asia Pacific LNG supplier and is committed to supplying the critical fuels such as oil and gas in a more sustainable way through decarbonising projects such as the Moomba CCS project. 


For more than 65 years, Santos has been working in partnership with local communities, providing local jobs and business opportunities, safely and sustainably developing its natural gas resources, and powering industries and households. 


 


What you’ll do:


Based in the field, the Senior Operator is responsible for leading the safe, reliable and efficient operation of onshore oil and gas production facilities. This role requires advanced technical knowledge and operational experience, enabling the Senior Operator to supervise plant activities, make operational decisions and support junior staff in achieving production and safety objectives.


The position is pivotal in maintaining asset integrity and optimising production performance. The Senior Operator also demonstrates leadership behaviours, serving as a role model for safe practices, operational excellence and continuous improvement.


 


Key accountabilities include:  




Operating production and utility systems safely, reliably and efficiently, ensuring compliance with procedures, permits and isolation standards


Undertaking Control Room Operator or Permit Authority responsibilities, including operational decision-making and coordination during normal and abnormal situations


Supervising and mentoring Operators, providing guidance, training and competency support to build workforce capability


Conducting inspections, monitoring process parameters and initiating corrective actions to maintain plant performance and safety standards


Identifying, reporting and following up on operational risks, equipment defects and process deviations in a timely manner


Maintaining accurate operational records, reports and documentation to support compliance and continuous improvement initiatives


Participating in emergency response, incident investigations and operational audits to enhance safety and reliability outcomes


Leading or contributing to continuous improvement initiatives, identifying opportunities to optimise processes, reduce downtime and improve asset efficiency


Demonstrating leadership behaviours, fostering teamwork, accountability and a high-performance culture among operational staff


Achieving and maintaining 100% Competency Assurance sign-off and meeting performance and behavioural expectations for the Senior Operator role




 


What you’ll bring:


You will be experienced in:  




A minimum of ten years' experience in process plant operations


A minimum of two years' experience in process plant control room operations


Strong interpersonal and communication skills, including effective engagement, negotiation and influencing


Sound knowledge of the chemistry and physics governing process operations


Strong analytical, numeracy and problem-solving skills




Ideally, you will also bring experience as a Supervisor within a Major Accident Hazard facility. You will hold a trade or diploma qualification in an engineering discipline.


 


What you’ll get: 


Here, you’ll be amongst high-calibre people and get to work on industry-leading projects. We don’t shy away from solving tough problems at pace. We like it that way. You can expect to be challenged and supported; to learn and grow.


At Santos, we’re committed to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive. This means a place that is safe; where you are valued and respected, and your contribution is recognised and appreciated. Join us, and you’ll play a role in this too.


Each of our sites offer access to specific amenities that aim to create the best possible benefits to your health, wellbeing and performance.


 


What you’re part of:


Everywhere you turn you will be a part of a team who are coming together to contribute to our single uniting purpose  - to provide reliable and affordable energy to help create a better world for everyone And because it’s not only what you do, but how you do it, you will also contribute to improving the living standards of the communities where we operate, building enduring and respectful relationships that serve a generation. It’s about each of us, and all of us – together.


 


How to Apply


Applications must be submitted via the online recruitment system before 
COB Friday 23 October 2026
.  


A requirement of this role is that you will need to have in place the legal work rights for PNG to apply. 


  


Potential Scams


There are a number of fake adverts that are impersonating Santos Limited, in these instances you will receive an e-mail from a generic e-mail address. We do not make offers without interviews or due diligence taking place.  You will know if an advert is genuine if you are directed to the Santos company careers page to apply which is 
https://recruitment.santos.com/





    	        
Apply

28809.description:
Lecturer Theology- School of Humanities, Education & Theology


The Organisation:


Pacific Adventist University (PAU) is owned and operated by the South Pacific Division of the Seventh-day Adventist Church. The institution is accredited to the Adventist Accreditation Association, an international denominational authority for all tertiary and graduate educational programs and institutions owned by the Seventh-day Adventist Church entities. The main campus is located on the pristine Koiari Park, 14 miles outside Port Moresby, the capital of Papua New Guinea. The institution was established in 1984. Since then, it has grown from a college of 20 students to a university of over 1000 students from across the Pacific.


The Role:


The Lecturer is responsible for teaching and learning activities at both undergraduate and postgraduate levels, including the supervision of honours and postgraduate research students. The role involves significant contributions to curriculum and course development, subject coordination, and the performance of administrative responsibilities within the school. The role is also expected to actively engage in scholarly, research, and professional activities, providing leadership in advancing academic excellence, research outcomes, and the overall reputation of the School and University.


 


Core Responsibilities:


 




Deliver learning experiences for students in a variety of settings which may include lectures, seminars, tutorials, practical/laboratory classes, demonstrations, workshops, field excursions, and clinical sessions.


Prepare/organise teaching/learning materials such as subject outlines, lecture notes, laboratory manuals, and audio-visual/multimedia aids.


Contribute to the ongoing development and quality assurance of subjects and courses.


Prepare, administer, and mark assessment instruments/tasks in accordance with the procedures outlined in subject outlines and in accordance with University policies and procedures.


Develop and maintain professional competence by participation in scholarly and professional activities such as research and publication, attendance/participation at academic conferences, membership of professional associations, networks with other academics, artistic exhibitions, musical performances, consultancies etc.


Attend convocation, graduation, staff meetings, and professional development activities; serve on University committees as requested; promote the University; and be conversant with, and follow, University policies and procedures.


Participate in School activities as requested by the Dean of School. This may include activities outside of normal class hours.


Meet deadlines relating to the submission of subject outlines, examinations, grades and other essential matters as requested.


Provide appropriate counsel and guidance to students, commensurate with the lecturer's expertise.


Participate in selected activities relating to the spiritual, cultural and/or recreational life of students on campus that reflect the lecturer’s interests and/or expertise.


Promote ethical behavior and Christian growth in both professional and extracurricular involvement with students and colleagues.


Maintain positive interpersonal relationships with teaching colleagues and other University staff.


Extend the influence of the University by involvement in the wider community.




 


About you: 


Qualifications:




A doctoral or master’s qualification appropriate to the relevant discipline area or equivalent accreditation and standing; and


A record of research/creative works or professional activity relevant to the discipline area, which demonstrates a capacity to make an autonomous contribution.


The capacity to undertake teaching autonomously at a high standard is essential.




Knowledge and Skills:




Deliver innovative, engaging, and challenging teaching that maximises student learning and is informed by sound scholarly practice.


Collaborate effectively with colleagues to support, develop, and promote high-quality and ethical research.


Foster a positive workplace culture that balances high performance with a harmonious and constructive environment.


Promote and model the University's philosophy, mission, values, and objectives through teaching and professional conduct.


Demonstrate a strong commitment to Jesus Christ and the mission of the Seventh-day Adventist Church.


Work effectively and respectfully within diverse and cross-cultural environments.


Possess the appropriate qualifications, skills, and professional competencies required for the relevant academic rank.




 


If you feel you are the right person for the role and you meet the minimum requirements above, you may request a ‘Position Description’ and ‘Application Form’ from the Human Resource Department via 
[email protected]
 . It is a requirement that ‘application forms are to be completed in full and that all supporting documentation including updated CV and copies of educational qualification be submitted also. As an equal opportunity employer, PAU particularly encourages applications from male applicants.


 


Application closes on Friday 23rd of October,
 2026.


 


All applications are to be addressed to:


The Human Resources Department


Pacific Adventist University


Private Mail Bag, Boroko, National Capital District


Email: 
[email protected]
 





            

        
Apply

28713.description:
OFFICE/DIVISION: 
     Office of the Vice President, Academic Affairs


POSITION TITLE: 
        Administrator, Learning Management System


POSITION NUMBER: 
    WPUVL002


POSITION CLASSIFICATION: 
    Academic


JOB LOCATION: 
                    Ialibu, Western Pacific University


ORGANISATIONAL RELATIONSHIP:


Immediate Supervisor: 
       Vice President, Academic Affairs


Supervises: 
                       Academic staff


Coordinates with: 
             Other Department Heads, Registrar, Vice Presidents for Academic, Finance, and Administration


JOB PURPOSE:


The Administrator, Learning Management System guides the development and implementation of short and long-range plans in conjunction with the Vice President Academic Affairs and the Faculties Deans for achieving WPU objectives to become a Virtual University while staying in alignment with the University digitalization strategic plan. Organizes initiatives for online programming and identifies trends in online learning including hybrid, distance learning, and fast track programming.
Directs the implementation of the WPU online digital learning platform and collaborates with the Vice President Academic Affairs and the Faculties Deans to ensure that students have access to the WPU core curriculum, databases and lecturers support.


DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES


1. Monitors the development and implementation of all aspects of the virtual learning process.
2. Provides administrative support for the online, virtual, blended, hybrid, and distance learning programme of Faculties (for example, student discipline, parent concerns).
3. Manages and provides leadership into WPU's Learning Management System in trainings and workshops.
4. Serves as liaison to online, virtual, blended, hybrid, and distance learning students, Faculty, staff, and WPU's educational leadership.
5. Establishes and monitors communication systems for lecturers, instructors, students, and families regarding student progress and programme updates.
6. Oversees and directs allocation of resources with the assistance and oversight of the Vice President University Advancement.
7. Monitors compliance with WPU University Council, Academic Board policies, State laws as they apply to virtual learning, curriculum, and instructional materials.
8. Maintains open lines of communication with all interested parties and responds to concerns of parents, lecturers, provincial, district office administrators and community members in a timely manner.
9. Maintains an accurate database, files, attendance records, and academic progress of students in virtual academy as required by the University.
10. Maintains compliance with National policies related to virtual learning and teaching and WPU requirements.
11. Conducts ongoing needs assessments, collects and analyzes data, and uses pertinent data to refine and improve the academic programmes.
12. Plans, implements and facilitates professional development/inservices for program staff.
13. Coaches, develops schedules, and works in conjunction with the Vice President Academic Affairs and Director of Human Resources in using an evaluation checklist for lecturers and the Learning Management System (LMS).
14. Assists to recruit, hire, and support lecturers and support staff.
15. Supervises and evaluates all assigned staff.
16. Provides leadership in the development of strategic approaches for the integration of technology into the educational environments of all WPU academic programmes.
17. Involves with the planning of instructional technology resources, focusing on the pedagogical use of various instructional technologies needed for online and face-to-face course deliveries.
18. Provides a strong ability to troubleshoot computer software and technology problems.
19. Represents the online and distance learning interests of all WPU academic programmes in regional meetings.
20. Fosters collegiality and team building among full and part time online certified and classified staff.
21. Works with others in a positive, productive way.
22. All other duties as assigned by the Vice President Academic Affairs, such as teaching and facilitating learning for students.


Online Course Design and Implementation


1. Coordinates instructional design with an understanding of best practices for virtual distance learning.
2. Works closely with Curriculum, Instruction & Assessment Specialists and campus Faculty to continuously assess online, virtual, blended, hybrid, and distance learning education initiatives and outcomes.
3. Maintains a high level of credibility by keeping up with the changes in all subject areas, ensuring online students receive similar learning opportunities as students in a classroom.
4. Coordinates academic programmes – building teams and distributing updates to all.


QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE


Qualifications


1. Minimum Master's Degree, preferably a PhD or Doctorate in an appropriate field.
Knowledge
1. In managing people.
2. ICT learning and teaching, fluent in speaking and writing English.
3. Understanding of Papua New Guinea culture or the ability to quickly understand the culture and adapt accordingly.
4. Knowledge of the academic environment and its role in society.


Skills


1. Computer literate (MS Word, Excel, email).
2. Skills working as part of a team.
3. Demonstrates leadership capacity.
4. Organisational and administrative ability.
5. Ability to liaise with key stakeholders in the community/industry to determine society's needs.
6. Ability to respond appropriately in the academic environment.


Work Experience


1. Experience as a Lecturer in a tertiary institution with five (5) years of online teaching and/or managing virtual learning environments.


Academic Publications


1. Published in professional journals within the country.


 


How to Apply


If then interested, all candidates must send their Expression of Interest, CV, and relevant documents to 
[email protected]
  / 
[email protected]
.


All corresponding emails must have in their subject 
“Position Description: [Position Title]”
 — e.g. 
“Position Description: Research Coordinating Officer.”


All application documents must be merged into one (1) PDF file before submission.


Attention to: 
Human Resources Director, P.O. Box 1791, Mt. Hagen, Western Highlands Province.


 


Applicants are encouraged to submit their application via email.


 


Applications close: 23rd October 2026, 4:06 PM


 


Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.





    	        
Apply

ORGANISATIONAL RELATIONSHIP:


Reports to:   
                                   Mathematics Lecturer


Supervises:   
                                  None


Coordinates with: 
                          Colleagues in Department


JOB PURPOSE:


The Tutor in Mathematics assists the Mathematics Lecturer in delivering high-quality instruction, fostering analytical thinking, and advancing mathematical knowledge through teaching, research, and academic service. The role supports student success and contributes to curriculum innovation in pure and applied mathematics.


DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES


Teaching & Instruction


1. Assist the Mathematics Lecturer in delivering engaging lectures, tutorials, and workshops in areas such as algebra, calculus, statistics, discrete mathematics, and mathematical modeling.
2. Develop and update course materials, assessments, and digital learning resources.
3. Supervise undergraduate and postgraduate research projects.


Curriculum Development


1. Design and revise mathematics curricula to reflect current academic and industry trends.
2. Integrate technology and software tools (e.g., MATLAB, R, Python) into teaching.


Research & Scholarship


1. Conduct original research in pure or applied mathematics and publish in peer-reviewed journals.
2. Collaborate on interdisciplinary research projects and seek external funding.


Student Support


1. Provide academic advising, mentoring, and support to students.
2. Encourage critical thinking, problem-solving, and independent learning.


Academic Service


1. Participate in departmental meetings, committees, and quality assurance processes.
2. Contribute to outreach activities and community engagement in mathematics education.


REQUIREMENTS AND QUALIFICATIONS


Education


1. Bachelor’s degree in Mathematics, Applied Mathematics, or a closely related field.
Experience
1. Prior tutoring, teaching assistant, or peer-mentoring experience is preferred.
2. Strong academic record in mathematics coursework.


Skills


1. Solid understanding of core mathematical concepts and problem-solving techniques.
2. Ability to explain mathematical concepts clearly to students at different levels.
3. Basic proficiency in mathematical software and tools (e.g., MATLAB, R, Python) is an advantage.


Attributes


1. Passion for mathematics and helping students learn.
2. Patient, approachable, and supportive of student needs.
3. Ability to work collaboratively within the department.

OFFICE/DIVISION: 
               Office of the Vice President, Academic Affairs


POSITION TITLE: 
                  Senior Instructional Designer


POSITION NUMBER:
               WPUVL003


POSITION CLASSIFICATION:
   Academic/Administration/U3.1


JOB LOCATION: 
                     Ialibu, Western Pacific University


ORGANISATIONAL RELATIONSHIP:


Reports to: 
                           Director, Virtual Learning


Supervises:
                           Instructional Designer


JOB PURPOSE:


The Senior Instructional Designer will lead the learning content and activity design and the development of materials as required by each project and will play a vital role in ensuring the development of content is relevant to the learning cohort, high quality and developed within the required timeline and the scope of the project. The Senior Instructional Designer will develop content in consultation with Lecturers and Content Experts and coordinate work to complete the learning design required by the stakeholders using a variety of methods and tools to deliver effective educational experiences across multiple platforms.


DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES


The Senior Instructional Designer (SID) is responsible for leading and managing the analysis, planning, design, development and implementation of all Virtual Learning initiatives in alignment with strategic and operational goals for course development. The Senior Instructional Designer will lead the effort to create innovative education solutions using sound instructional design methodologies, current technologies and effective project management to meet organizational product development goals.


Instructional Design


1. Lead the development of instructional materials, such as courses, eLearning modules, and instructor-led training (ILT) programs.
2. Utilize proven instructional design models (e.g., ADDIE, SAM) to create impactful learning experiences.
3. Create detailed storyboards, curriculum, and assessments for learning modules.
4. Ensure content is engaging, interactive, and aligns with the organization's goals and objectives.


Needs Assessment


1. Conduct comprehensive needs assessments by collaborating with stakeholders, subject matter experts (SMEs), and learners.
2. Analyze data and feedback to identify performance gaps and learning needs.
3. Translate business objectives and learner requirements into clear, measurable training goals.


Project Management


1. Manage multiple instructional design projects simultaneously while meeting deadlines and quality standards.
2. Work with cross-functional teams to ensure timely delivery of learning materials.
3. Track and report on project milestones and performance metrics.


Technology and Tools


1. Design and develop eLearning modules using tools like Articulate Storyline, Adobe Captivate, or similar platforms.
2. Integrate multimedia elements (videos, graphics, simulations) to enhance learning experiences.
3. Leverage Learning Management Systems (LMS) to deploy and track training programs.


Collaboration and Stakeholder Engagement


1. Partner with SMEs, trainers, and other stakeholders to gather content, feedback, and resources.
2. Provide guidance to junior instructional designers or team members as needed.
3. Present design concepts and training plans to management and other stakeholders.


Evaluation and Continuous Improvement


1. Evaluate the effectiveness of training programs using surveys, assessments, and feedback.
2. Use data to refine and improve learning solutions, ensuring continual alignment with organizational needs.
3. Stay updated on best practices, trends, and emerging technologies in instructional design.


REQUIREMENTS AND QUALIFICATIONS


a. Bachelor's or Master's degree in Instructional Design, Educational Design or E-learning is desirable.
b. At least 5 years of experience in instructional design, with a proven track record of designing and developing training programs with elements of open, distance and technology mediated learning.
c. Proficient with eLearning development tools (LMS platforms).
d. Strong project management skills, including the ability to manage multiple projects with competing deadlines.
e. Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills.


 


How to Apply


If then interested, all candidates must send their Expression of Interest, CV, and relevant documents to 
[email protected]
  / 
[email protected]
.


All corresponding emails must have in their subject 
“Position Description: [Position Title]”
 — e.g. 
“Position Description: Research Coordinating Officer.”


All application documents must be merged into one (1) PDF file before submission.


Attention to: 
Human Resources Director, P.O. Box 1791, Mt. Hagen, Western Highlands Province.


 


Applicants are encouraged to submit their application via email.


 


Applications close: 23rd October 2026, 4:06 PM


 


Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

OFFICE/DIVISION:   
                Office of the Vice President, Research & Innovation 


POSITION TITLE:
                       Research Coordinating Officer to the Director of the Department for Social Sciences Research


POSITION NUMBER: 
                  WPUEXPR006


POSITION CLASSIFICATION:
     Grade 15 – Social Science


JOB LOCATION:
                         Ialibu, Western Pacific University 


ORGANISATIONAL RELATIONSHIP:


Reports to:   
                         Director of Social Sciences Department
Supervises: 
                          Researchers, Research Technical Staff.
Coordinates with: 
                Director of Sciences Research Department, Director of Contract & Consultation Research Department, and Director of Faculty Research.


JOB PURPOSE:


The Research Coordinating Officer operates under general direction of the Director of the Social Sciences Department, performs duties associated with coordinating, implementing and balancing multiple research studies and projects. The Research Coordinating Officer is accountable to deliver established goals, utilizes good judgment, knowledge and skills in the area of expertise while maintaining expected quality standards.
This job description does not include every duty that an individual in a position performs. It is intended to be representative and characteristic of the duties required and the level of work performed. Depending upon the size of the Department and its functional activities, incumbents who fall into this category may perform all of the duties listed below or, in the case of large Departments, may be assigned to designated specialized functions.


DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES


1. Regular attendance is an essential requirement of the position.
2. Assists research personnel in the implementation of research studies to ensure successful completion of study goals.
3. Prepares and maintains Departmental Board and regulatory e-work to comply with University regulatory requirements.
4. Assists in the recruitment and relationship building of study subjects, arranges study visits and provides instructions to meet the goals of the study.
5. Abstracts or collects data from study subjects and enters information into the designated forms/database to comply with study protocols.
6. Maintains inventory of supplies or equipment, prepares study kits and requisitions prior to study visits to ensure the appropriate items are available when necessary.
7. Builds and maintains a broad network of professional relationships with participants, principal investigator, co-investigators, research study staff, and other collaborators to ensure successful research collaborations.
8. Identifies and reports issues that may affect the accuracy and quality of study design and implementation to meet study aims.
9. Participates in internal/external research related conferences and investigator meetings to build and maintain relationships.
10. Reports as required by internal Research Division policies.
11. Performs other duties as assigned by the Director.


REQUIREMENTS AND QUALIFICATIONS


a. Master's Degree in a relevant field of study.
b. Requires 4 years of relevant experience.
c. Working on research contracts within a Higher Education environment.
d. Working effectively and flexibly as a member of a team.
e. Working in a client focused environment and meeting client needs.
f. Communicating complex information to non-specialists.
g. Working independently and proactively.
h. Working with high levels of accuracy and with attention to detail.
i. Writing/developing material for the web.
j. Research law, particularly intellectual property, confidentiality, publications and indemnity.
k. Proven ability to understand and interpret complex documentation. Proven ability to understand, interpret, apply and develop policies and procedures related to research.
l. Excellent oral and written communication skills.
m. The ability to use judgement, initiative and creativity to identify and solve complex problems.


 


How to Apply


If then interested, all candidates must send their Expression of Interest, CV, and relevant documents to 
[email protected]

.


All corresponding emails must have in their subject 
“Position Description: [Position Title]”
 — e.g. 
“Position Description: Research Coordinating Officer.”


All application documents must be merged into one (1) PDF file before submission.


Attention to: 
Human Resources Director, P.O. Box 1791, Mt. Hagen, Western Highlands Province.


 


Applicants are encouraged to submit their application via email.


 


Applications close: 23rd October 2026, 4:06 PM


 


Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

                                     None


JOB PURPOSE:


The Lecturer in Information Technology will contribute to the university’s academic mission by delivering high-quality teaching, conducting impactful research, and engaging with industry and community partners. The role supports the development of digital competencies and innovation across undergraduate and postgraduate IT programs.


DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES


Teaching and Learning


1. Deliver lectures, tutorials, and practical labs in core IT areas such as programming, databases, networking, cybersecurity, cloud computing, and software engineering.
2. Design and assess assignments, exams, and capstone projects in line with academic standards.
3. Supervise student research, internships, and final-year projects.
Curriculum Development
1. Contribute to the design and continuous improvement of IT curricula to reflect emerging technologies and industry needs.
2. Integrate modern tools and platforms (e.g., Git, AWS, Docker, Python, Java, SQL) into course delivery.
Research and Innovation
1. Conduct original research in areas such as artificial intelligence, data science, human-computer interaction, or systems development.
2. Publish in peer-reviewed journals and present at academic conferences.
3. Seek external funding and collaborate on interdisciplinary research initiatives.
Student Engagement and Support
1. Provide academic advising and mentorship to students.
2. Foster a supportive and inclusive learning environment that encourages innovation and critical thinking.
Professional and Community Engagement
1. Build partnerships with industry, government, and professional bodies to enhance teaching and research impact.
2. Participate in outreach activities, guest lectures, and community-based projects.
Academic Service
1. Contribute to departmental governance, accreditation, and quality assurance processes.
2. Serve on academic committees and participate in strategic planning.


REQUIREMENTS AND QUALIFICATIONS


Education
1. A Master’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, or a related field is essential.
2. A PhD or progress toward a PhD is highly desirable.
Experience
1. University-level teaching experience in IT or related disciplines.
2. Demonstrated research output or industry experience in IT.


Skills

2. Strong communication, presentation, and interpersonal skills.
3. Ability to use learning management systems (e.g., Moodle, Canvas) and online teaching platforms.

OFFICE/DIVISION: 
    Western Pacific University’s Office of the Vice President, University Advancement


POSITION TITLE:
        Fixed Asset & Inventory Officer


POSITION NUMBER:
    WPUFD010


POSITION CLASSIFICATION:
    Administration


JOB LOCATION: 
           Western Pacific University, Ialibu, SHP, PNG


ORGANISATIONAL RELATIONSHIP:


Reports to:
     Bursar


Supervises:
      None


Coordinates with:
   Accounts Payable, Purchasing Officer, Heads of Departments, Directors, Executive Officers, and various Officers.


JOB PURPOSE:


The Fixed Asset & Inventory Officer supports the Bursar in the delivery of efficient and effective fixed asset and inventory management services to the University. The Fixed Asset & Inventory Officer supports the Bursar in ensuring that the University has a functioning asset and inventory management framework, including relevant policies and processes, and in the efficient delivery of asset and inventory management services.


DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES


1. Ensure all tasks are completed in accordance with the relevant work schedule.
2. Support the implementation of the University's fixed asset and inventory management plans.
3. Ensure the University's asset management programs are delivered in accordance with budget allocations.
4. Ensure asset management processes are in compliance with relevant strategies, policies and statutory regulations.
5. Review and draft policies on matters relating to fixed asset and inventory management.
6. Assist in reviewing and updating procedures and systems to ensure high quality asset management services.
7. Review and update the asset register for the University and ensure that the asset management database is maintained regularly.
8. Receive, inspect and store incoming goods and equipment, checking deliveries against purchase orders and packing documentation.
9. Conduct regular stocktakes and cycle counts, always with a second staff member present, and promptly reconcile any discrepancies.
10. Monitor stock levels against usage patterns and set reorder points to prevent shortages or overstocking.
11. Manage expiry dates and stock rotation (FEFO/FIFO) and ensure storage and handling practices meet safety requirements for all inventory, particularly sensitive and time-limited items.
12. Ensure appropriate security practices are maintained for all inventory and fixed assets to prevent shrinkage and unnecessary write-offs.
13. Identify stock or assets that are obsolete, expiring, near expiry, or damaged, and recommend appropriate action.
14. Analyse usage and forecast requirements to ensure inventory is maintained at optimal levels, and take stock of assets and inventory, formulating related reports.
15. Track equipment usage, location, condition, labelling, and servicing/warranty dates, and coordinate repairs, maintenance or replacement of equipment with relevant stakeholders.
16. Assist with the annual fixed assets audit and prepare reports for fixed asset verification.
17. Prepare regular reports on inventory status, stock levels, stock movements and discrepancies to support decision-making.
18. Coordinate with Accounts Payable, the Purchasing Officer, Heads of Departments, Directors, Executive Officers, and various Officers on asset and inventory matters.
19. Participate in gender equity/equality and other institutional wellbeing activities that will assist the University to address these issues.


REQUIREMENTS AND QUALIFICATIONS


a. Bachelor's Degree in Accounting, Finance, or Management; a Master's Degree is a bonus.
b. A minimum of four (4) years of experience in fixed asset and inventory management.
c. Strong data analytical skills and inventory management skills.
d. Able to work well with colleagues, respond to requests in a timely manner and share relevant information with the Division, the University and with other stakeholders.
e. Able to contribute to identifying team priorities, share or allocate specific tasks within the team, and ensure competing deadlines are met.
f. Able to contribute, as required, to identifying divisional and University strategic goals and budget plans, and assist in the preparation of related documentation.
g. Ensure all expenditure, acquittals and other financial and commercial transactions strictly adhere to University and Government-wide policies and/or legislation.
h. Establish knowledge about the range of Acts, laws and policies governing the work of the University.
i. Demonstrate and practice high levels of integrity, honesty, accountability, respect and wisdom, and accept responsibility for one's own actions at all times.
j. Demonstrate substantial proficiency in the use of email and internet, and in the application of software such as MS Word, MS Excel and MS PowerPoint.
k. Understanding of Papua New Guinea's public procurement and tender laws, including the National Procurement Act 2018 and the Public Finances (Management) Act 1995.
l. Experience with computerised inventory/stock management systems is an advantage.
m. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with strong numeracy and accurate record-keeping skills.
n. Able to use initiative and problem-solve, with a proactive and adaptable approach to work.


 


How to Apply


If then interested, all candidates must send their Expression of Interest, CV, and relevant documents to 
[email protected]
  / 
[email protected]
.


All corresponding emails must have in their subject 
“Position Description: [Position Title]”
 — e.g. 
“Position Description: Research Coordinating Officer.”


All application documents must be merged into one (1) PDF file before submission.


Attention to: 
Human Resources Director, P.O. Box 1791, Mt. Hagen, Western Highlands Province.


 


Applicants are encouraged to submit their application via email.


 


Applications close: 23rd October 2026, 4:06 PM


 


Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.
