28773.description:
POSITION TITLE:
  
NURSE SPECIALIST SUPERVISOR – Banz Jiwaka Province


CONTEXT


Médecins Sans Frontières (Doctors Without Borders) is a private, non-profit international humanitarian organization, founded in 1971 and working in 70 countries around the world. MSF provides medical assistance to populations in crisis, regardless of race, religion, belief, or political affiliation. In PNG, MSF has been working since 2007 in Lae, Tari, Bougainville, Gulf Province, and NCD Province. MSF is now working to support the Department of Health to improve access to care for patients in JIWAKA and LAE.


 


JOB PROFILE:  


REPORTING LINE :
  Project Medical Referent, MSF JIWAKA PROJECT


Is responsible for the technical support for the Village health Volunteers – VHVs, maintenance replenishment  and replenishment and organization of the medical Items and the supervision of village health volunteers within the community as a  technical physician in the field, according to MSF protocols, values, universal hygiene standards and community needs in order to provide a high-quality care to the survivors of violence patients




Reporting to, communicating and collaborating with the Health Promotion team in order to ensure the smooth and efficient running of the Decentralized model of care at the community level, according to the protocols outlined for the community services. Working together with all health promotion teams to achieve quality care for survivors of violence within the community. Always maintaining patient’s confidentiality and dignity and respecting the survivor’s rights and conditions, being compassionate to the survivors of violence needs.


Maintaining the organization of the community services, which includes defining the daily, weekly and monthly programs in collaboration with the health promotion team, anticipating the needs and adapting the planning as required. Planning and delegating the tasks to the HP team members when not available, ensuring that the tasks are accomplished and checking that the team are respecting their work schedule. Coordinating with all the medical departments involved with outreach and community activities (laundry, stretcher bearers, surgical wards and ER, etc. Recognition of survivors, PFA, referral to the next level of care, provision of EC and FP contraceptive pills, provision of male/female condoms, basic first aid and wound care, identification of danger signs) to ensure quality and quantity of supply and timing.


Ensuring the general organization of the department, checking that care protocols and rules on security, hygiene and sepsis are followed by the health care and maintenance personnel and monitoring the quality of the global patient case management and the continuity of care. Participating in the medical community outreach activities in order to meet with the survivors and follow the activity more closely. Encouraging daily health education sessions on the basis provision of health needs within the community in case of injuries


Supervising and supporting the team under his/her responsibility e.g. the VHVs, Planning and organizing their work (areas, days, absences, visits, holidays, etc.) and coaching them in their work with special focus on following all appropriate protocols and procedures.


Ensuring the quality of care by respecting and ensuring respect of MSF community approach and involvement and proposing action plans to ensure the quality of hygiene, and respect of procedures. Evaluating the implementation of first aid care procedures by doing regular assessments and informing the Nurse of the assessment results and of any problems.


Ensuring that the VHV using medical items are qualified and trained. Ensuring cleaning and maintenance tasks are performed according to the protocols. Reporting any shortages of items in the kit to the supervisor for possible refill.


Managing the village health volunteers’ stock and weekly and monthly orders. Ensuring the follow up of the consumption of medical first aid kits under his/her responsibility and ensuring that data collection sheet is well fulfilled and kept


In close collaboration with the HR department, supervising the associated HR processes (recruitment, training, induction, evaluation, potential detection, coaching, development and communication) in order to ensure both the sizing and the amount of knowledge required.


Ensuring that all the administrative procedures, patients’ data and documents are filled in correctly and registered for compiling monthly reports reflecting the activity in the department. Participating in the collection and analysis of medical data, identifying areas causing problems and implementing the necessary measures for the improvement of the service’s functioning.




 


 


The districts of operation: South Waghi, North Waghi, Anglimp and Jimi district including  other Provinces that shall be explored including community health post within the catchment areas


Primary Goal: 
Established a proven Decentralized model of care – DMC that can easily be adopted by the PHA. Oversee and supervise the medical activity Outreach in close collaboration with Health Promotion team, build the capacity of the village health volunteers and CHW, on all forms of violence through mentorship and training.


Specific Tasks of the Nurse Specialist Supervisor 




Establish pathway to community access to medical care especially after violence for the medical care and referral and provide information for legal redress.


With VHV and CHW, develop community approaches especially at community health post to develop support a Foot Patrol service that enhances minimal medical services provision in the community like provision of; PEP, EC pills, ORS, case identification, PFA, referrals and provision of first aid care in the community.


Develop a medical intervention plan in cases of community conflicts that result in severe injuries and that require medical attention within the community. And create clear referral pathways for the community to access medical services (e.g.: scoop and run approach, primary trauma care that can be adapted)


In collaboration with HP supervisor and team leader/officers, enhanced the capacity of Village Health Volunteers (VHV) and Community Health Workers (CHW) to support the Foot Patrol activities in the community.


Readiness to address infrastructural issues like privacy and confidentiality, of all medical files of patients, ensure referrals of patients affected by Violence and those who require special medical/legal attention are referred to the designated department


Working closely with the medical team to ensure documentation of medical records meets the required standard and that medical files are kept confidential but in line with PHA protocols


With OIC in each district assured that there is compliance/adherence of treatment such as PEP follow-up, STI treatment while engaging the staff and addressing their challenges


Engage the OIC in the FSC setting to identify training needs for Nurses, VHV and CHW in the community health post for better service delivery and good orientation of the medical team.


Provide support to PMR when engaging with other stakeholders and the PHA to strengthen good working partnership and collaboration meetings.


With support from PMR and Mission Pharma, analyze the availability of specific medicines and medical supplies at the health facilities we are supporting. Specifically, Describe the burden of morbidities related to violence (number of cases seen monthly and annually, describe the supply chain and describe the gaps in items or quantities to help in determining MSF donation strategy through either gap fill or buffer stocking


Participate in the definition and development of the pharmacy donation strategy for the MSF supported health facilities or catchment areas


National Staff Health: Take note and ensure record of the staff on follow-up with specialist in the designated health facilities (LHS) when sick, have list of staff who need frequent follow-up with their physicians, then inform the PMR, making sure staff are supported and sent to the designated hospital assigned by MSF for medical care. All medical certificates will be directly brough to PMR for strict confidentiality and staff data protection.




Documentation and Reporting




Ensure that all administrative procedures and documents are completed correctly according to the National guidelines and/or MSF Guidelines, whichever is applicable.


Compiling and analyzing monthly reports


Ensure that the confidentiality of any survivor of violence is kept in a locked cupboard to ensure their information is securely stored.


Participate in the weekly medical meeting and monthly reporting and discussion of the project.




 


SKILLS AND QUALIFICATIONS










 












Local language essential (Tok Pidgin), knowledge of mission language (English)


Key competencies: commitment, flexibility, results-oriented, stress management, and teamwork, Reliability, discipline, and respect for procedures are critical behavioral competencies.


Registered Nurse (diploma essential) with at least 
2 years
 of experience as Nurse, having been a nurse supervisor is an asset.

.

PHA

Government Health facility
 .


Desirable experience in 
MSF
 or other 
INGOs, NGOs. 
 


Essential computer literacy (word, excel, PowerPoint, internet, outlook).


Strict adherence to MSF policies, including zero tolerance for alcohol consumption during working hours.




 










 


WORKING CONDITIONS
           




Full-time position with an open-ended contract.


Based in Banz, Jiwaka Province with frequent visits to project areas (Family Support Centers, Health Posts & Health Centers) in Jiwaka Province.


Candidates must be flexible with working hours and location.




 


APPLICATION PROCESS


The applicants must send their 
Cover letter
 with an 
updated CV
 and a copy of any other relevant documents 
(Diplomas
, 
Certificates
, 
License
, 
Work Certificates
, 
Reference Letter
s) to:


 










By hand:


Médecins Sans Frontieres France


Jiwaka Mission Resort


Banz Dona road, portion 52


Banz, North Wahgi District 281 PG

Please clearly indicate in your application the position title and your phone number.  No document will be returned. 
Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted
. Please note that 
MSFF does not provide transportation or accommodation
 for the written tests and interviews. Written tests and interviews will be held in Banz, Jiwaka Province.

MSF is focused on ensuring that only those who share and demonstrate our values are recruited to work with us. To ensure we meet these standards, MSF has a “zero-tolerance” to any kind of abuse, exploitation, harassment and inappropriate behaviours.


MSF is committed to safeguarding, protection and fulfilling duty of care to patients, all people and communities we serve, and our staff. All staff are required to share this commitment through signing and complying with our Behavioural Commitments and all relevant safeguarding policies. 


Furthermore, receiving MSF job offers will be subject to satisfactory professional reference checks and clean criminal clearance.


MSF is an equal opportunity employer and does not charge any application, recruitment, or training fees at any stage of the process.

Job Type:
 
Permanent
 
About us 


K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate. 


We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.


About the role


This position is responsible for carrying out electrical breakdown and preventative maintenance repairs on a wide range of mobile equipment including Light Vehicles, Truck fleet, Excavators, and support equipment.


Key Accountabilities




Performing scheduled and Breakdown maintenance on a large fleet of Surface Mining Equipment including Sandvik Drills, Trucks and Loaders with an ancillary fleet of CAT and Volvo equipment.


Conduct regular electrical tests and tagging on equipment’s and machines.


Direct and train subordinates to install, maintain or repair electrical wiring, equipment’s, and machines.


Maintain safety work standards in accordance with government regulations and company policy.




About You 


To be considered for this role, it is essential that you must have a NATTB certified Trade certificate in Auto-electrical with at least 3-5 years of relevant work experience in heavy industry preferably mining environment. In addition to this, you will have some or all the following.




Demonstrated experience in maintaining electrical equipment in the mobile fleet including Trucks, Loaders, Light vehicles, Dozers


Relevant experience in automotive air conditioning systems.


Self-motivated with ability to always work autonomously.


Strong safety focus and sound knowledge of standard operating procedures.




Life at K92

Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.

28760.description:
Report directly to the CEO and help shape strategy for lasting community impact
Lead a district team and build local capability that outlasts the programs
See your work change lives across Western Province communities
Lead change where it matters most | Daru, Western Province, PNG | Senior Leadership Role
   
 
Shape the future of Western Province
 Our client is a leading development organisation working to build healthy, educated and resilient communities across Western Province. Through long-term partnerships and investment, it delivers multi-sector programs in health, education, livelihoods, agriculture and fisheries, and small business development, reaching some of Papua New Guinea's most remote and underserved communities. Its approach is built on genuine partnership with government and communities, so that the benefits outlast the programs themselves.
   
 
The opportunity
 This is a rare chance to sit at the heart of a development organisation and connect its programs with the government systems and communities they serve. Reporting directly to the CEO, you will lead the Program Coordination Unit and its district team. You will oversee the district program portfolio and make sure provincial, district, LLG and ward planning and budgeting work hand in hand with program delivery.
   
 You will be the organisation's voice in the districts and the community's voice inside the organisation. You will build trusted relationships with government leaders, agencies, churches, women's and youth groups, and development partners, and turn those relationships into joint planning, co-investment and stronger local systems. If you want your leadership to leave something lasting behind, this is the role.
   
 
What you'll be doing
 
 
Strategic leadership:
 Advise the CEO and senior leadership team on program design, community expectations and emerging risks. Identify opportunities for growth, innovation and impact.
 
Local systems strengthening:
 Mobilise local government for joint planning, budgeting, co-contribution, monitoring and governance. Support capacity building that improves service delivery on the ground.
 
Partnerships and negotiation:
 Negotiate and manage MOUs, co-funding arrangements and partnership agreements. Secure and protect land agreements that underpin program delivery.
 
Program portfolio oversight:
 Build and maintain a district-level portfolio management and reporting system. Review and approve implementation work plans, and help Pillar Leads deliver on time, on budget and to standard.
 
Community expectations and grievances:
 Manage stakeholder expectations, resolve grievances within policy timeframes, and advise on safeguards and cultural fit.
 
Financial oversight:
 Develop and manage annual district budgets in line with delegated authority and financial policy.
 
People leadership:
 Lead, mentor and develop District Managers and Coordinators, building a safe, inclusive, high-performing team culture.
 
Governance and compliance:
 Uphold safeguarding, child protection, gender equality, environmental and contractual obligations, with zero tolerance for fraud.  
 
 
What you'll bring
 
 
A bachelor's degree in Development Studies, Public Administration, Project Management, International Development, Social Sciences or a related field
 
A minimum of 10 years' senior management experience in the not-for-profit, development, government or humanitarian sector
 
Proven multi-sector project management experience in remote or rural settings
 
Demonstrated experience working with PNG's provincial, district, LLG and ward planning, governance and budgeting systems.
 
Strong experience working with subnational government, agencies, communities, donors and development partners
 
Demonstrated experience overseeing budgets, organisational planning, strategy implementation and performance management
 
Experience negotiating complex stakeholder environments, community interests and land-related matters will be highly regarded.
 
Political astuteness, resilience and adaptability, with a leadership style that empowers teams and earns the trust of communities
 
A genuine passion for improving livelihoods and service delivery in underserved communities  
 
 
Ready to make an impact?
 If you are a seasoned development leader who knows how to bring government, communities and partners to the same table, and you want your next role to leave a real mark on the lives of thousands of Papua New Guineans, we want to hear from you.
   
 Apply now with your CV and a cover letter outlining how your experience matches this role by 
COB Friday 16th October 2026
. To apply, upload your documents via the ‘APPLY NOW’ button
Peopleconnexion PNG: Recruitment, Training, Immigration, Payroll & HR Services.
www.peopleconnexion.com/png
Your legacy is our business





    	        
Apply

POSITION TITLE:
  
Drivers (3) – Banz Jiwaka Province 


CONTEXT


Médecins Sans Frontières (Doctors Without Borders) is a private, non-profit international humanitarian organization, founded in 1971 and working in 70 countries around the world. MSF provides medical assistance to populations in crisis, regardless of race, religion, belief, or political affiliation. In PNG, MSF has been working since 2007 in Lae, Tari, Bougainville, Gulf Province, and NCD Province. MSF is now working to support the Department of Health to improve access to care for patients in JIWAKA and LAE.


 


JOB PROFILE:  


REPORTING LINE :
  Logistics Supervisor, MSF JIWAKA PROJECT


Performing the tasks of transporting authorized goods and passengers in an 
MSF
 vehicle, ensuring its technical and safety conditions, and respecting the country's traffic rules and 
MSF
 security rules, in order to provide a safe, smooth, and efficient service.




Checking daily, the technical conditions of the assigned vehicle (state of the tires, oil, fuel, brakes, radio equipment, spare parts, etc.), performing weekly check according to the MSF Logbook, refilling it when necessary, and keeping it clean to ensure it can be driven in perfect condition. Carrying out a handover if another person uses the vehicle.


Ensuring the security of passengers in the vehicle, driving carefully, observing speed limits and traffic rules in the country as well as MSF security rules, to avoid car accidents.


Ensuring all passengers have all necessary papers in order before travelling and ensuring non-MSF staff sign disclaimers of responsibility before using the vehicle.


Ensuring correct loading and unloading of the vehicle, submitting the documents to the receiver of the goods, check-in the status of delivered goods, returning the duly completed documents to Logistics and ensuring that the goods have the necessary documents.


Ensuring that all vehicle documents and the driver's driving license are valid and in the vehicle.


Informing the line manager of any incident involving the transportation of passengers and/or goods


Knowing how to use all types of radios, codes, call numbers and radio alphabets by heart and communicating with base according to MSF communications policy to inform the driver's position and any potential implications.


Knowing and respecting the security rules related to vehicle movements, specifically those related to customs, checkpoints and roadblocks. Ensuring all passengers know and respect the security rules.




 


Drive with 
extreme caution
, especially in 
Banz’s and Jiwaka’s high-risk areas
, following MSF and local traffic safety regulations.


Ensure the 
security of passengers
, confirming that all MSF protocols are respected (e.g. seatbelts, door locks, restricted routes)


Remain alert to 
local security risks
, including roadblocks, carjacking hotspots, and gang-related violence.


SKILLS AND QUALIFICATIONS










 












Local language essential (Tok Pidgin), basic knowledge of mission language (English)


Key competencies: commitment, flexibility, results-oriented, stress management, and teamwork, Reliability, discipline, and respect for procedures are critical behavioral competencies.


Essential literacy and a valid PNG driving license. Good knowledge of Jiwaka Province and Country roads.


Essential 2 years of driving experience, especially 4x4 vehicles, Proficient in both manual and automatic vehicle operation.


Desirable experience in MSF or other NGOs


Essential knowledge of basic mechanics


Experience driving in rural high-risk environments (Jiwaka Province ) is an asset.


Strict adherence to MSF policies, including zero tolerance for alcohol consumption during working hours.

Cover letter

 and a copy of any other relevant documents

,

Work Certificates

Reference Letter
s) to:

The Role


Reporting to Chief Executive Officer, the General Manager – Corporate Services is a full-time, on-site role based in the National Capital District, Papua New Guinea. This position oversees core corporate functions, including human resources, Facilities, administration, and compliance, ensuring they operate efficiently and align with the company’s strategic goals. Day-to-day responsibilities include leading and mentoring corporate services teams, managing budgets and resource allocation, monitoring performance metrics, and implementing policies and procedures that support effective operations. The General Manager will coordinate cross-functional initiatives, maintain strong internal controls, and ensure adherence to regulatory and governance requirements. The role also involves preparing executive reports, supporting senior leadership in decision-making, and driving continuous improvement across corporate services.


 


In This Role, You Will




Provide overall leadership for the Human Resources function, including workforce planning, recruitment, employee relations, and performance management


Lead the development and consistent application of HR policies, procedures and employment documentation, ensuring compliance with Papua New Guinea employment legislation


Provide strategic direction for family welfare, liaison and support services for employees and their families, including relocation, settlement and community integration


Oversee the safe, efficient and professional operation of PNG Chiefs’ facilities and accommodation, including maintenance, bookings, and service provider relationships


Support operational planning for the Centre of Excellence and other current or future PNG Chiefs’ facilities


Build and lead an effective Corporate Services function, including budgets, procurement, contracts and reporting


Ensure effective coordination between HR, welfare, facilities, finance, security and other business functions


Contribute to organizational strategy, annual planning, workforce design and long-term capability development as a member of the Senior Management Team


Provide trusted advice to the CEO and Senior Management Team on people, welfare, facilities and governance matters




 


About You


You are a motivated and experienced leader with a strong background in corporate services, human resources, operations, or administration. You are a strategic thinker, a strong people leader, and a trusted business partner who can build effective teams, improve systems, and drive organizational performance. You are adaptable, culturally aware, and excited by the opportunity to contribute to the growth and success of the PNG Chiefs.


 


Qualification




Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Management, Commerce, Law, or a related discipline.


Minimum of 5 years' experience in a senior management or corporate services leadership role, with responsibility for people, operations, facilities, administration, or related business functions.


Proven experience leading multidisciplinary teams and supporting organizational growth in complex or evolving environments.


Experience working across diverse cultural settings, ideally within the Pacific region, developing markets, or comparable international environments.


Demonstrated ability to establish and improve systems, policies, and operational frameworks within a growing organization.

28759.description:
Newmont produces metals the world needs - safely, responsibly and with care for people, communities and the environment. With a 100+ year history, we continue to shape the future of mining through innovation and strong operational performance. By joining our inclusive, world-class team, you can help shape the future of mining and make a meaningful difference.


 


Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.


 


We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.


 










Your Impact






As an Advisor, People Case Management, you'll plan and conduct Tier 2 ‘Respect at Work’ workplace investigations for the business unit, helping ensure workplace standards, policies and the Code of Conduct are upheld. You'll investigate concerns, assess information and findings, and support fair and respectful workplace outcomes.










As Part of Our Team, You Will






•    Plan and conduct Tier 2 workplace investigations and related activities, including interviews, analysis and assessment of information and evidence.
•    Serve as a key contact for employees and stakeholders during assigned investigations, supporting professional and respectful interactions throughout the process.
•    Prepare investigation reports, and communicate findings and recommended actions to appropriate stakeholders.
•    Maintain accurate investigation records and provide advice on corrective measures arising from investigation findings.
•    Identify process and control gaps, improvement opportunities and training needs, while supporting awareness of the Code of Conduct, policies and workplace standards.










Prerequisites for Your Success in This Role








Knowledge of HR/People practices, workplace policies, procedures and standards, with the ability to apply them fairly and consistently.


Experience conducting workplace investigations, including interviewing, assessing information and drawing evidence-based conclusions.


Ability to navigate difficult conversations and conflict while working compassionately, fairly and respectfully with people involved in cases.


Strong written communication skills, with the ability to sift through detailed information and prepare clear reports, findings and recommendations.


MS Office skills and the ability to build effective working relationships with a diverse range of people and stakeholders.












Your Work Environment






This role is offered on a 21:21 Fly-in, Fly-out (FIFO) roster to Lihir Island, Papua New Guinea.


Our FIFO employees stay in a secure and comfortable camp environment, with ensuite, air-conditioned accommodation equipped with a mini fridge, television and Wi-Fi. A variety of nutritious meal options are available through the on-site catering facilities, while recreational and social amenities provide opportunities to relax and connect with colleagues while on roster.


You'll work with the onsite People team and people leaders on workplace investigations, while building stakeholder relationships and developing familiarity with the business, investigation processes and expectations for a respectful workplace.










Why Join Newmont






Lihir is one of the world's largest producing gold mines and one of Newmont's most significant operations.


Working at Lihir means joining a high-performing team committed to safety, operational excellence and delivering sustainable value for our people, communities and business. 


Eligible employees may benefit from:
•    Competitive salary and annual performance incentive opportunities.
•    Company-funded FIFO travel and modern camp accommodation.
•    Access to health, wellbeing and employee assistance programs.
•    Ongoing learning, technical development and leadership training opportunities.
•    Exposure to large-scale mining operations and industry-leading technologies.
•    Career opportunities across Newmont's Australian, Papua New Guinean and global operations.
•    Access to a diverse range of on-site recreational, dining and wellbeing facilities.
•    The opportunity to be part of a workplace where safety, inclusion and growth are at the centre of everything we do. 


Submit your application through our website quoting reference number 44964 before the advertised closing date: 16 October 2026.












At Newmont, our people are our strength and we’re committed to a safe, inclusive and supportive workplace. If you’re passionate about doing work that matters, join Newmont and help shape the future of mining.​






Learn more about our purpose and values: 
About Newmont
​
Hear from our people: 
Life at Newmont
​






Important: Newmont does not ask candidates to pay money or share sensitive personal data outside our secure application process. If this happens, please report it to our Business Integrity team: 
[email protected]
.




 







    	        
Apply

ATMI Engineering Services Ltd.
 is seeking a motivated, organised and safety-focused 
HSEQ Coordinator
 to join our team and support our construction, electrical, mechanical, maintenance and project operations.


The successful candidate will work closely with Project Managers, Supervisors and workers to help ensure HSEQ requirements are understood, implemented and maintained throughout project execution.


 


WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR


We are looking for someone who is proactive, reliable, technically competent, organised and accountable. The successful candidate must be able to assess planned work activities, identify hazards and determine the appropriate Risk Assessment, JSEA/JSA, SWMS, PTW and activity-specific permits without requiring step-by-step direction from Management.


 


KEY EXPECTATIONS




Plan and prepare HSEQ requirements before mobilisation.


Work closely with Project Managers, Operations and Site Supervisors to understand the actual work methodology and site conditions.


Ensure HSEQ documentation is complete, reviewed, approved and available before deployment.


Conduct site inspections, inductions, toolbox meetings and pre-start briefings.


Ensure workers understand and acknowledge applicable HSEQ documentation and controls.


Enforce compliance and exercise Stop Work Authority where necessary.


Professionally coordinate HSEQ requirements with clients and principal contractors.

28727.description:
Executive Assistant to the Vice-Chancellor


 


The Organisation:
 


Pacific Adventist University (PAU) is owned and operated by the South Pacific Division of the Seventh-day Adventist Church. The institution is accredited by the Adventist Accreditation Association, an international denominational authority for all tertiary and graduate educational programs and institutions owned by the Seventh-day Adventist Church entities. The main campus is located on the pristine Koiari Park, 14 miles outside Port Moresby, the capital of Papua New Guinea. The institution was established in 1984. Since then, it has grown from a college of 20 students to a university of over 1000 students from across the Pacific. 


 


The Role:


The Executive Assistant provides high-level administrative, organizational, and governance support to the Vice Chancellor. This role ensures the efficient operation of the Vice Chancellor’s office by managing schedules, communications, documentation, and stakeholder engagement, while modelling the values of Pacific Adventist University and contributing to its mission of excellence in education, service, and community engagement.


 


Core Responsibilities:
 




Manage the Vice-Chancellor’s calendar, appointments, and travel arrangements.


Screen calls, emails, and correspondence, ensuring timely responses and prioritization.


Prepare correspondence, reports, and official documentation with accuracy and confidentiality.


Prepare agendas, minutes, and follow-up actions for meetings., especially AdCom and Council meetings and other governance bodies in consultation with the Vice Chancellor.


Ensure timely distribution of governance documents and follow-up on action items.


Maintain filing systems (hard copy and electronic) for confidential documents and records for governance and compliance purposes.


Draft, proofread, and distribute official correspondence, notices, and reports.


Oversee office supplies, memberships, and professional affiliations.


Organize and manage events hosted by the Vice-Chancellor’s Office.


Support graduation ceremonies especially with graduation refreshment, official visits, and university-wide functions.


Collaborate with other executive offices for joint events and public relations.


Act as the primary point of contact for internal and external stakeholders engaging with the Vice Chancellor’s office.


Draft professional correspondence and manage sensitive communications with discretion.


Organize and coordinate official meetings, workshops, and University events involving the Vice Chancellor.


Provide logistical and administrative support during high-level engagements.


Represent the Vice-Chancellor’s Office with diplomacy and professionalism.


Assist in monitoring key projects and initiatives aligned with the university’s mission.


Provide research, briefing notes, and background materials for executive decision-making.


Manage and run PAU transits.




 


About you:  


 


Qualifications and Skills required: 




Active relationship with Jesus Christ, characterised by a deep desire for worship and service to God.


Baptised membership in the Seventh-day Adventist Church with a deep commitment to its educational philosophy and mission.


A Diploma or Degree in Office Administration, Business or any related field from a recognised institution.


Proven ability to maintain confidentiality and handle sensitive information.


Minimum of 5 years’ experience in executive-level administrative work.


Demonstrated ability to manage confidential information with integrity.


Strong organisational, time management and multitasking skills.


Excellent written and verbal communication skills.


Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite.


A sound working knowledge of, and proven loyalty to, the church, its organisation and policies.


Have an interest in and aptitude for cross-cultural ministry.


Excellent event management skills.


Ability to liaise confidentially with all the Government departments, corporate clients and the general public on behalf of the Office of the Vice-Chancellor.


The ability to work unsupervised and responds effectively to dynamic institutional needs.


Manages multiple priorities with accuracy and efficiency.


Produces clear, structured, and polished written and verbal communication.


Proven ability to maintain the highest level of confidentiality, integrity, and ethical standards.


Builds positive relationships across diverse internal and external audiences.


Excellent interpersonal skills.


High level of integrity and commitment to ethical standards.


Commitment to the mission and values of Pacific Adventist University

Reporting to the General Manager – Marketing and the General Manager – Communications & Media, you will lead the club's public relations activity and deliver events that bring the Chiefs brand to life - from media conferences and sponsor functions to match-day activations, community programs and fan events. 27706.description:
Job Type:
 
Permanent
 
About us 


K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate. 


We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.


About the role


In this role you will provide management and leadership within our mobile maintenance department. This rewarding role will see you provide daily mentoring, guidance, instruction, and training to the national workforce to increase safety performance, machinery uptime and efficient outcomes within a motivated and talented department.


Key Accountabilities




Coordinate workshop activities through the Mobile Maintenance Supervisors.


Give direction, delegate tasks and provide technical assistance to subordinates.


Liaise with senior maintenance leadership on planned maintenance.


Maintain stock levels and place orders as required.


Ensure cost control measures are considered by utilizing resources available to full capacity.


Report and rectify any hazardous sightings to the Mobile Maintenance Superintendent in the 800L workshop.


Ensure training requirements are met.


Organise and document weekly safety toolbox meetings workshop safety representatives.


Regularly monitors and evaluates staff performance in consultation with Mobile Maintenance Superintendent.


Provide coaching for performance improvement.


In conjunction with mobile maintenance superintendent, takes disciplinary action to address performance deficiencies, in accordance with the Company’s rules, policies and procedures.


Personally, responds to inquiries and complaints from the employees.


Responds to emergency situations as necessary.


Carry out other relative duties as directed by the Mobile Maintenance Superintendent.


Maintain safety work standards in accordance with government regulations and company policy.


Perform all roles and responsibilities that support and reflect the company’s mission and core values.




About You 


Qualifications & Experience




Relevant trade qualification in Heavy Equipment Fitting, Auto Electrical and Automation. Minimum Certificate III required.


10+ years relevant work experience essential.


Underground mobile fleet such as Sandvik and Caterpillar and provide guidance of Methods, practices, techniques.


Ability to plan, assign, direct and coordinate a variety of functional specialties (areas) with overlapping work areas.


Must have at least 5 years in mobile fleet maintenance in a supervisory capacity. Should also have experience in training of both operating and maintenance personnel.


Experience in the use of Pronto will be advantageous.


Sound planning, analytical and problem-solving skills.


Excellent trouble shooting skills.


Self-motivated with the ability to work under pressure and autonomously.


Excellent attention to detail and time management skills to meet deadlines.


Strong active listening & interpersonal skills for rapport building, conflict resolution & training.


Actively promotes a safe and healthy culture.




Life at K92  


K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.


Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.


At K92, we want all employees to share in our success, so as well as a competitive salary, employees also participate in our long- and short-term incentive plans, we also provide employees with access to savings incentive programs, medical assistance and the option to salary sacrifice for certain expenses.


In addition to all of this, employees can also access our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.


 
THIS POSITION IS OPEN ONLY TO CANDIDATES WHO HAVE THE RIGHT TO LIVE & WORK IN PNG WITHOUT SPONSORSHIP 





    	        
Apply

28895.description:
Position Title: Boiler Operator


Location: Madang 


Division: Globe


 


Overview
We are seeking a skilled and safety-conscious Boiler Operator to ensure the safe, efficient, and compliant operation of our site’s boiler systems and associated utilities. You will be responsible for maintaining continuous steam supply to production lines, monitoring boiler parameters, performing routine maintenance, and ensuring compliance with PNG safety regulations and internal policies.


 


Key Responsibilities
Boiler Operation & Monitoring: Operate, monitor, and control boiler systems to ensure consistent steam supply for production. Conduct routine checks on pressure, temperature, water levels, fuel supply, and safety devices.


Record Keeping: Record operational data in logbooks and digital systems. Maintain accurate maintenance records, daily logs, and incident reports.


Water Treatment & Quality Control: Monitor and maintain boiler water quality, including chemical dosing and blowdown procedures. Conduct water tests to prevent scaling, corrosion, and carryover.


Maintenance & Repairs: Perform preventive and corrective maintenance on boilers, feed pumps, valves, burners, and water treatment systems. Troubleshoot mechanical, electrical, and control issues affecting boiler performance.


Safety & Compliance: Ensure all boiler operations comply with PNG safety regulations and internal policies. Maintain and test safety valves, alarms, gauges, and emergency shutdown systems.


Communication & Coordination: Report abnormalities, breakdowns, and potential risks to the Utilities Supervisor. Liaise with production teams and maintenance staff to coordinate shutdowns and repairs.


Cross-Functional Support: Assist with other utilities systems such as air compressors, generators, and refrigeration units when required.


 


Qualifications
Trade Certificate or Qualification in Mechanical Engineering, Fitting & Machining, or a related field.


PNG Boiler Operator Certification (Class 1 or Class 2) is essential.


Minimum 3 years’ experience operating industrial boilers (fire-tube or water-tube).


Strong understanding of boiler safety standards and water treatment processes.


Knowledge of Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) regulations.


Ability to read and interpret technical manuals, gauges, and instrumentation.


Good verbal and written communication skills.


PNG National Driver’s License is desirable.


 


Work Environment


Industrial manufacturing setting with exposure to heat, steam, noise, and rotating machinery.


Requires use of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) and strict adherence to safety protocols at all times.


May require shift work, including nights, weekends, and public holidays.

Champion a strong safety culture by leading hazard identification, risk management, and safe work practices across the team.


Develop and execute weekly maintenance plans, ensuring resources are effectively allocated to achieve operational targets safely and efficiently.


Actively contribute to pre-starts, production, maintenance, and planning meetings to align priorities and drive team performance.


Provide visible leadership in the field, guiding the team through critical daily maintenance activities and operational challenges.


Step into the Supervisor role as required, ensuring continuity of leadership and safe execution of work.


Lead engaging pre-start meetings that reinforce safety expectations, priorities, and team accountability.


Partner with Operations to prioritise breakdowns and coordinate resources to deliver timely, safe, and effective maintenance solutions.


Apply your knowledge of oxygen plant operations and cryogenic systems to support safe, reliable, and efficient plant performance.


Play a key role in shutdown planning, readiness, and execution, ensuring work is completed safely, on schedule, and to the highest standards.




About You




Trade-qualified Turner/Fitter with a recognised NATTB trade certificate.


Demonstrated experience in a similar role within cryogenic plant environments
Strong commitment to safety, with a solid understanding of hazard identification and risk management processes.


Proficient in Microsoft Office applications, including Excel and Word, with the ability to maintain accurate records and reports.


Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively across teams and stakeholders.




Working Conditions
This is a FIFO role on a 21/21 roster.

28730.description:
MARINE LIVELIHOODS OFFICER


 


The Wildlife Conservation Society (WCS) is an international non-governmental organisation committed to working with communities, government, and other partners to manage wildlife and wild places for biodiversity and human well-being.


WCS PNG seeks a dynamic 
Marine Livelihoods Officer 
to design, implement, and support community-based livelihood initiatives that strengthen household resilience while reducing pressure on biodiversity. Reporting to the Program Manager, the position is full-time and based in Kavieng, New Ireland Province.


Main Responsibilities: 




Conduct assessments to understand livelihood needs and opportunities in partner communities, focused on marine and coastal livelihood interventions, including small-scale fisheries and seafood products.


Lead implementation of nature-positive livelihood interventions through ongoing projects


Document impacts of livelihood interventions, including but not restricted to yields, sales and profits.


Support and conduct training on family business management, financial literacy and other appropriate topics.


Work closely with the other WCS teams to embed livelihood activities within or alongside environmental management and conservation activities with communities.


Work with partner communities and LMMAs to widen the impact of livelihood interventions.




Ensure livelihood interventions are inclusive and culturally appropriate




Translate technical and scientific information into simple English and Tok Pisin to enable easier comprehension for those with low literacy skills.


Provide capacity building to local staff and partners.


Represent WCS during stakeholder and partner engagement and outreach meetings, workshops and conferences.




 


Qualifications and Experience




Bachelor's degree in a relevant field (e.g., Marine Resource Management, Environmental Science, Development Studies, Fisheries, or related discipline) is preferred. However, candidates with substantial relevant experience in livelihoods development projects, particularly in marine and coastal settings, will be given equal consideration.


At least two years’ full-time professional experience in implementing marine and coastal-focused livelihood projects with the private sector and non-governmental organization (NGO) or a government agency or equivalent


Strong understanding of and experience conducting financial and business management training for communities


Good interpersonal skills and experience in liaising with a range of stakeholders, including traditional landowners, local and state government, special interest groups and individuals regarding natural resource management issues.




 


Critical Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities




Experience in community engagement, facilitation, and participatory planning.


Experience working with communities, and customary institutions.


Strong facilitation and conflict-sensitive communication skills.


Understanding of social safeguards, inclusion, and gender-sensitive approaches.


Ability to work respectfully within diverse cultural contexts.


Excellent computer literacy and skill of MS Office applications (Word, Excel and PowerPoint) and the /internet)


Good analytical and problem-solving skills


Good knowledge of written and spoken English and Tok Pisin


Strong interpersonal skills and emotional intelligence


Being a self-starter with drives and initiative, and able to work as a team or an individual with a positive attitude and open minded


Excellent organisational and leadership skills


Excellent communication skills


Ability to work with less supervision and under pressure




 


Application Process:




Applications should be submitted only by email to 
[email protected]
 by 5 pm on 14
th
 October 2026.


Submit your CV (3 pages maximum) and a cover letter (2 pages maximum) as one combined PDF file with the following naming system: “first name last name GEDSI & MEL Officer.pdf”, with the email subject as “Application for Marine Livelihoods Officer: first name last name”


Only list full-time, paid positions in your CV, starting with your current or last position and going backwards.


Do not submit any other documents, including reference letters, transcripts, diplomas, etc. with your application.


Cover letters and CVs generated with AI may be rejected at the discretion of WCS.




 


Applications will be evaluated on a rolling basis. We encourage you to submit your application at the earliest.


 


 


WCS is an equal opportunity employer, and the organisation complies with all employment labor laws and regulations that prohibit discrimination in hiring, ensuring that candidates from all backgrounds are fairly and consistently considered during the recruitment process. We are dedicated to hiring and supporting a diverse workforce. We are committed to cultivating an inclusive work environment and look for future team members who share that same value. The organisation provides equal employment opportunities for all qualified candidates. The organisation does not discriminate for employment based on age, colour, disability, gender identify, national origin, race, religion, sexual orientation, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by laws and regulations


 


 








Apply

28720.description:
POSITION DESCRIPTION










TITLE






WASH TECHNICAL OFFICER










REPORTING TO






WASH ADVISOR










LOCATION






WEWAK










CLASSIFICATION






D1 










EMPLOYMENT DETAILS/HOURS






Permanent, 
one -year contract (possible extension)










 


Introduction


 


WaterAid’s vision is of a world where everyone has access to safe water and sanitation. Our mission is to transform lives by improving access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) in the world’s poorest communities. WaterAid works with partners to maximise its impacts for policy change/influence.


 


WaterAid works through supporting local organisations and government authorities to design and demonstrate appropriate and sustainable WASH programs. WaterAid also seeks to influence policy change through government and other key sector actors to secure and protect the right of poor people to safe, affordable water and sanitation services.


Everything we do is shaped by our six values:




Integrity


Respect


Collaboration


Courage


Accountability


Innovation




 


WaterAid has been operating in Papua New Guinea (PNG) since 2004, working with local partners and the government to increase access to gender sensitive, socially inclusive and climate resilient water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) services. WaterAid PNG’s geographic focus is on the National Capital District and Central Province in the Southern Region, East Sepik Province and East New Britain Province.


WaterAid works through supporting local organisations and government authorities to design and demonstrate appropriate and sustainable WASH programs. WaterAid also seeks to influence policy change through government and other key sector actors to secure and protect the right of poor people to safe, affordable water and sanitation services.


WaterAid is a child safe organisation. We recognise that we must meet community expectations, and the trust placed in our personnel to maintain the highest standards of conduct with children. Therefore, all positions within WaterAid are required to comply with our Child Safeguarding Policy and Code of Conduct.


 


WaterAid is committed to protection from sexual exploitation and abuse in everything we do. The values and standards we uphold are highlighted in our Global Code of Conduct. All positions within WaterAid are required to comply with our Global Code of Conduct.


 


WaterAid passionately believes everyone in the organisation has a role to play in innovation, encourages curiosity about the world and empowering everyone to act. We recognise that both big and small changes can have positive impacts on our roles, our team and our mission.


 


Position Summary


 


WaterAid is committed to supporting the Government of PNG to have an inclusive and climate resilient Water, sanitation and hygiene services. The WaSH Technical officer is a highly capable individual that supports the implementation and contractor supervision for WaterAid’s infrastructure projects in delivering WASH hardware outcomes through inclusive and equitable water, sanitation and hygiene.


The WASH Technical Officer will be a member of the WaterAid Wewak Programs Team reporting to the WaterAid Wewak Project Coordinator & WaSH Technical Advisor. The officer will receive technical support and mentoring from the WaterAid WaSH Technical Advisor.


The position will focus mainly on the Advancing Quality Universal Access (AQUA) to WaSH project to improve health outcomes in the Wewak District of the East Sepik Province.  Wewak, , The project aims to improve health outcomes by increasing access to clean, safe and reliable water sources in communities and HCFs across East Sepik Province. By focusing on target districts, including Wewak district, the project aims to catalyze sustainable WASH system improvements, advancing the Wewak District WASH Plan (2024 – 2027).


The position is key to deliver the technical hardware WASH component of the The Coca Cola Foundation (TCCF) funded project in the final year of implementation.


 


Key Performance Areas/Accountabilities


 




Project Management 






Work with the WASH Technical Advisor, Wewak Program Coordinator and Program Officers to prepare and deliver project implementation plans that take into account project/grant requirements, partner engagement and capacity, and good development practice (sustainable, collaborative, empowering, rights based).






Implement WaSH infrastructure programme plans through project site visits scheduled, alongside other WAPNG staff. This will include community engagement, WASH and health education, interactive WASH workshops and WASH infrastructure delivery.


Contribute to programme implementation, development and reporting within frameworks and methodologies including but not limited to, National WaSH Policy, WASH in School Policy & Infrastructure Guidelines, Community Led Total Sanitation (CLTS) and Gender Equality, Disability and Social Inclusion principles (GEDSI), WaterAid PNG Water Quality Testing Policy, WaterAid PNG Health & Safety Policy & Guidelines, etc. 






Ensure that the projects satisfy minimum criteria defined in respective WaterAid Guidelines and PNG Government policy, law and regulation, and are implemented in line with grant requirements, budgets and plans, including by overseeing work of construction partners. Simultaneously, use the WA Expenditure Tracker to manage the funds on a weekly basis.


Conducting project baseline and endline assessments of infrastructure projects to inform the design of contextually appropriate WaSH infrastructure, for tracking project and program outputs and the uploading data onto WAPS under the framework on weekly, monthly and quarterly basis.


Supporting the design of appropriate, cost effective, sustainable and inclusive WASH infrastructure that responds to local contextual factors.


Provide support to the WaSH Technical (Infrastructure) Team in the development of accurate bills of quantities and costing.


Where necessary, arrange meetings with WaSH Committees/partners/contractors to agree on designs, construction approaches, negotiate contracts, build capacity of construction partners and local technician in the community, monitor progress of infrastructure construction; identify and manage any risks.


Provide support to the WaSH Technical Advisor to develop sound contract agreements with successful contractors to implement WaSH infrastructure projects.


Ensure WaSH Advisor & Wewak Programs team is kept informed of activity progress, risks and all relevant issues always by sending reports, messages on WhatsApp group and updating project status on WaterAid Project Systems (WAPS) on a weekly basis.


Work with respective Program Officers & Coordinators to provide support to the WaterAid team on hygiene and sanitation behaviour change approaches and support the team to ensure ‘good practice’ approaches are always pursued.


Ensure timely submission of payment requests & advances, processing of acquittals and follow up with partners/contractors for finance documentation as needed.  Ensure activities are implemented in accordance with the design, scope of work and available budget.


Support procurement of goods and services required for infrastructure projects adhering to WaterAid procurement & finance processes.  This includes initiating cost estimates for review and submission to line manager for review where necessary.


Respond to requests for information promptly and accurately.


Conduct formative research on hygiene and sanitation and support the design of activities that aim to change practices when required.


Ensure water quality testing is carried out for all WaterAid Projects and results communicated and uploaded to WAPS. Conduct frequent rapid testing at project sites as needed.


Comply with contextualised WA standard Occupational Health & Safety and Operations & Maintenance are adhered to in project implementation. 


Lead, supervise and work alongside casually engaged local artisans and general labour ensuring casuals’ well-being is addressed. This includes ensuring all casuals undergo safeguarding training and other mandatory WA awareness & training sessions before their engagement.




 




Monitoring, Evaluation, Knowledge and Learning




 




Monitor and support implementing partners (contractors) and staff to ensure that construction is of high-quality standard and consistent with their contractual obligations and plans. This includes routine monitoring and supervision for casual engaged artisans and tradesman.


Ensure WaSH Advisor & Programs team are kept informed of activity progress, risks and all relevant issues always by sending reports, messages on WhatsApp group and updating project status on WaterAid Project Systems (WAPS) on a weekly basis.


Responsible for collecting and maintaining accurate data to support reporting and reviewed in the MEL framework in WaterAid Programme System. Ensure the data reported in the framework, indicators and results in WAPS


Support the Programs Team to facilitate information gathering activities related to the collection or development of baseline data, case studies and research.


Lead the review of the data in WAPS and upload all the data for baseline, endline and research into WAPS on annual basis


Coordinate and compile technical reports on WaSH infrastructure to contribute to timely reporting, communication and learning for WaterAid (internal), donors, partners and stakeholders.


Regularly report to the line manager on all relevant matters including, but not limited to, programme updates, programme developments and progress, programme issues such as resourcing needs, training/development, leave, work, health & safety issues.




 


Attend and participate in all scheduled or mandatory meetings, training and activities


 




Equity and Inclusion




 




Ensure that WaterAid’s WaSH infrastructure work is inclusive in design, with consideration to women, girls, people with disabilities   and other marginalised groups in design and implementation.


Support the GEDSI team upload and review the risk data into WAPS and monitor on a regular basis.


Identify opportunities to further engage the community in the planning, monitoring and review of WASH services and work with local authorities and community representatives to design and implement feedback mechanisms about community access to water, sanitation and hygiene services.


Build the capacity and understanding of the WaterAid Team on gender, equity and inclusion and how to ensure WaterAid programs are inclusive.


Consult with the GEDSI Advisor on the equity and inclusion aspects of the work and ensure that WaterAid staff and external stakeholders are sensitive to gender and social inclusion considerations.


Promote a ‘Do No Harm’ approach amongst WaterAid staff and partners and ensure that referral pathways are accessible for stakeholders and beneficiaries affected by WaterAid’s work.             




 




Partner Engagement






Build and maintain constructive working relationships with WaterAid’s local partners. Mentor and support WaterAid Team members to do likewise.


Coordinate field visits with partners with sensitivity to security and accessibility issues.


Support WaterAid to undertake due diligence assessments on all new /potential contractors and to take forward corresponding development plans.


Represent WaterAid through local sector coordination bodies where required.




 


Communications & Working Relationship.


 


 
Internal




WaterAid PNG- Programs & Operations-Finance


WaterAid Australia (participation in learning events, liaising with technical leads & Advisors where required.)


WaterAid global intranet (participation in webinars and other online learning platforms)




 


External




Multiple governmental and non-governmental stakeholders


Contractors


Good and Service providers


Casual Artisans




 


 


 Physical environment & Demands


 




High travel requirements within Wewak & Maprik Districts of East Sepik province potentially with potential travel to other WaterAid office sites where required.




 










Qualification, Skills & Attributes (Key Capabilities/Selection Criteria)










Essential






 










Knowledge, skills and experience








Responsible for planning, designing and implementation monitoring of Water Supply and sanitation activities implemented by WaterAid and local partners or contractors.  


Assisting partners on technical surveys, design and preparation on cost estimating of WASH projects.


Lead & supervise construction and installation of WaSH infrastructure


Knowledge and Experience using AutoCAD in doing 2D and 3D drawing and uploading of all technical drawings to WAPS.


Conducting regular monitoring and providing technical feedback to the partners or contractors and relevant WA staff


Mentor and supervise casual staff and construction artisans on technical matters.


Skills and knowledge in facilitating training to colleagues, partner/community on technical matters.


Proactivity in taking necessary action to design cost effective, easy to maintain and easy to replicate the WASH components & technologies.


Ability to develop project implementation plans that align with grant requirements and available funding, and to plan own work, setting priorities and completing it under pressure or when faced with competing demands.


Experience in working constructively with government and partners to co-develop and implement water, sanitation and hygiene and advocacy projects.


Good relationship building skills.


Have at least experience working with one of the following approaches to sanitation and hygiene such as Healthy Islands, Community Led Total Sanitation, Participatory Hygiene and Sanitation Transformation.


Experience with the conduct of baseline & endline for hygiene and sanitation projects




--                 Commitment to child safeguarding.


--                 Sensitive and working to meet project timelines and deadlines.










Education






--        bachelor’s degree in technical field(s) of Building, Architecture, Engineering or a related field is advantageous. Minimum of 5 years’ experience in small to medium sized infrastructure projects with field experience is desirable.










Personal qualities






1.      Commitment to WaterAid’ values and standards of safety of children and protection from sexual exploitation and abuse in all our activities


2.      Demonstrate an understanding of gender equality and women’s empowerment including ethnic diversity and cultural sensitivity


3.      Demonstrated commitment to innovation and continuous improvement.


4. Eagerness & willingness to learn and participate in learning events, forums, online webinars & platforms.










Recruitment process


 


This position is open to Papua New Guinean candidates only


 


Applications for this role must comprise of:


 




An application letter addressing the essential person specification criteria outlined above (maximum 2 pages).


A curriculum vitae (maximum 4 pages). The CV must include three professional referees (referees will not be contacted until after interviews, with permission from the candidate).




 


Applications which do not address the Selection Criteria specified and the page limits will NOT be considered.
 


 


Late and incomplete applications will not be accepted.


 


WaterAid is committed to welcoming people from the widest possible diversity of backgrounds, culture and experience. Female candidates are strongly encouraged to apply. We will make any practical adjustments to enable people with a disability to participate fully in an inclusive working environment. Please let us know if require any special assistance in making your application or attending an interview.


 


Email applications to: 
[email protected]
 
with the subject line: 
“Application – WASH Technical Officer”
. The closing date is 14
th
 October 2026.


 


 


Please note that only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.


Note:
 WaterAid is a child safe organization. The successful applicant will be required to comply with our child protection policy.       








Apply

Urgent Hiring


PROPERTY SUPERVISOR 


JOB DESCRIPTION


This position requires an individual with high initiative attitude to deal with property- relevant matters.  The Property Supervisor is generally responsible for supervising properties of an organization and is very much knowledgeable in using personal computer (PC) as a main tool to communicate with property owners, clients / tenants, service providers and other staff. The Supervisor is responsible in finding tenants directly liaising with real estate agencies if needed.


 


RESPONSIBILITIES:




Oversee daily operations of residential and/or commercial properties.


Supervise Maintenance and cleaning staff, ensuring timely property upkeep


Handle tenants relations, including lease agreement, renewals and conflict solutions


Conduct property inspections to ensure compliance with safety and quality standards.


Coordinates repairs and maintenance with vendors and contractors.


Maintains safe and healthy work environment by adhering to legal standards and regulations


Responsible in developing schedules, assigning and monitoring work related to properties


Manage the company's vehicle fleet, including registrations, insurance, servicing, repairs, licensing, and fuel monitoring.


Recommends solution to problems related to properties as they arise


Responsible in looking out for tenants for vacated units.


Maintains good filing system of all properties. Prepare report on property condition.


Support leasing activities by assisting with tenants applications, move-ins and move-outs.




 


QUALIFICATIONS:




Male aplicants only


Preferably with certificate on Business Administration or related course


At least 3x years experienced in a supervisory position


With ability to find qualified tenants


Very knowledgeable in property handling i.e. leases, repairs, routine maintenance, security, etc.


Ability to handle multi tasks and work in fast-paced environment.


With driving skills and with valid driver’s license


With attention to detail


Excellent communication, organizational, negotiation, and problem-solving skills.

Accounting / numerical skills required


Very good customer service

28520.description:
Manage consolidation across multiple entities and markets
Drive general ledger oversight and reporting efficiency
Lead and develop a financial accounting team, including succession planning
The Company
 
 
Our client is a leading financial services organisation operating across the Asia-Pacific region. The organisation is focused on innovation, data modernisation, and delivering customer-centric solutions. It is committed to exceptional service for its customers and communities while fostering an environment where employees can grow and progress.
The Role
This Financial Reporting Manager role is responsible for leading the Group’s statutory reporting, financial consolidation, and general ledger governance. Reporting to the Head of Financial Reporting, you will ensure the accurate and timely delivery of consolidated financial statements and provide critical financial oversight across Pacific markets and subsidiaries.
Key Responsibilities
 
 
Manage the preparation and finalisation of month-end, half-year, and annual consolidated financial statements for the Bank and Group in accordance with IFRS.
 
Consolidate forecasts, budgets, and reforecasts for Pacific entities, and lead the preparation of high-level board papers and Executive Committee commentary.
 
Run the end-to-end audit process, including planning, technical responses, and coordination with external auditors.
 
Ensure strict adherence to International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS), BPNG Prudential Standards, and internal Bank policies.
 
Oversee the review of month-end journals, including IFRS 16 leases, write-offs, and recoveries.
 
Drive continuous improvement and process efficiency across the reporting cycle, assisting with system transformation projects.
 
Manage and mentor the Financial Accounting team, providing direction and building technical capability.
 
 
Qualifications, Skills & Experience
 
 
Tertiary qualifications in Accounting, Finance, or Business are essential.
 
Certified Practising Accountant PNG (CPA PNG) or equivalent certification is mandatory.
 
Minimum of 8 years’ experience in financial reporting or audit, with at least 3 years in a managerial or supervisory capacity.
 
Banking experience is highly desirable; however, broad corporate experience from mining or large corporate environments is also valued, provided you possess strong consolidation and ERP expertise.
 
Advanced knowledge of Financial Statement preparation (P&L, Balance Sheet, Cash Flow) and senior-level general ledger control.
 
Strong proficiency in ERP systems and advanced technical skills in Microsoft Excel and Word.
 
Excellent verbal and written communication skills to present complex financial information to diverse stakeholders.
 
 
To apply for this position, interested candidates are asked to submit:
 
 
A cover letter addressing key criteria of the role
 
An updated CV in Microsoft Word format, outlining employment history, educational qualifications, and listing three referees (referees will only be contacted if shortlisted)
 
 
Our client's priority is to provide opportunities to high performing Papua New Guineans for this position.  Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

www.peopleconnexion.com/png
Your legacy is our business
