28847.description:
Job Type:
 
Permanent
 
About us 


K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate. 


We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.


About the role


Joining our underground maintenance team, this role is responsible for the implementation and maintenance of mine power supply and distribution system for all electrical equipment on the mine and on our exploration sites in Kainantu. In addition, this position will also play an important role in the training of trades assistants.


Key Accountabilities




Inspect, isolate, and repair electrical malfunctions using various hand and power tools.


Ensure that alarms and emergency electrical systems onsite are always operational.


Direct and train subordinates to install, maintain or repair electrical wiring, equipment, and machines.


Diagnose electrical defects or hazards on systems, appliances and machinery and identify adjustment and repair timely.


Ensure that alarms and emergency electrical systems onsite are always operational.


Conduct regular electrical tests and tagging on equipment, appliances, and machines.


Inspect, test and qualified to apply and remove ‘out-of-service’ or ‘not-to-be operated’ tags to electrical equipment, appliances, and machines.


Prepare sketches and plan layout to determine the location of electrical wiring and equipment and to always ensure safety compliance.


Direct and train subordinates to install, maintain or repair electrical wiring, equipment, and machines.


Delegate routine tasks to subordinates and provide supervision where required.


Respond to routine and emergency calls for repair and service within the mine site area, underground and on field, or where job is required.


Work long and odd hours and often be on call in emergency situations and extreme conditions.


Attend to physically demanding tasks involving digging ditches and moving and lifting heavy objects.


Perform general housekeeping within and around work area.


Ensure and maintain safe work standards and practices in accordance with mine safety regulations for all tasks performed.


Maintain safety work standards in accordance with government regulations and company policy.


Perform all roles and responsibilities that support and reflect the company’s mission and core values.


Ensure that the sections daily work plans are executed as directed.


Competent in lifting and safe operation of workshop equipment.


Reading and understanding technical drawings and manuals.


Diagnose problems in all equipment with regular reference to equipment manuals.


Prepare and plan of welding jobs for site services.


Carry out equipment alignments with Dial Indicators.


Conduct accurate dimensional checks of crusher bushes, shafts or bearing clearances and recording data.


Attend to isolations required for simple tasks to major shutdowns.


Conduct general housekeeping at work area.


Identify and report safety hazards.


Maintain safety work standards in accordance with government regulations and company policy.


Perform all roles and responsibilities that support and reflect the company’s mission and core values.




About You 


To be considered for this role, it is essential that you have a NATTB Trade Certificate as well a current electrical license. You will also need to demonstrate experience in the installation and maintenance of power distribution systems, transformers, motor control centres and starters. In addition to this, you will have some or all the following.




Five (5) years’ experience working in a mining environment.


Maintenance of underground equipment – electric motors, compressor stations and other electrical equipment.


You must have a High Voltage switching ticket.


You must have a wide experience in installation and maintenance of Low and High Voltage transfers and starters. 


Must be a self-starter and very resourceful with ability to find solutions to problems to ensure the equipment availability is high.


Be flexible and adaptable to the needs of the business and ability to work harmoniously as part of the team.




Life at K92  


K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.


Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.


At K92, we want all employees to share in our success, so as well as a competitive salary, employees also participate in our long- and short-term incentive plans, we also provide employees with access to savings incentive programs, medical assistance and the option to salary sacrifice for certain expenses.


In addition to all of this, employees can also access our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster. 


THIS POSITION IS OPEN ONLY TO CANDIDATES WHO HAVE THE RIGHT TO LIVE & WORK IN PNG WITHOUT SPONSORSHIP 






Apply

Shipping Supervisor


Position Title:
 Shipping Supervisor
Reports To:
 Shipping Manager / National Manager
Department:
 Operations
Location:
 Port Moresby


 


Job Summary:


To supervise and coordinate all shipping and freight forwarding activities, ensuring import and export shipments are processed efficiently, documentation is accurate, CargoWise records are maintained, and customer service standards are achieved. The role is responsible for ensuring departmental KPIs are met while maintaining strong communication with customers, shipping lines, customs authorities, and internal stakeholders.


 


Key Responsibilities:




Supervise daily shipping and freight forwarding operations to ensure departmental KPIs are achieved.


Coordinate import and export shipments from booking through to final delivery.


Ensure MRNs and W&H invoices are issued within required timelines.


Ensure delivery orders are released promptly and purchase orders are raised within required timeframes.


Monitor shipment status and proactively communicate updates, delays, and operational matters to customers and stakeholders.


Liaise with shipping lines, shipping agents, customs authorities, transport providers, and clients on operational matters.


Ensure all jobs, milestones, costs, revenue entries, and shipment activities are accurately updated in CargoWise.


Monitor CargoWise job management, job profitability, invoicing, and monthly job closure.


Ensure shipping-related accounts and outstanding matters are reviewed and reported regularly.


Coordinate with Operations and Transport teams to ensure timely cargo collection and delivery.


Train, coach, and support team members to improve performance and service standards.


Ensure compliance with company procedures, customer requirements, and regulatory obligations.


Prepare shipping and operational reports for management.


Perform other duties as assigned by management.




Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)




Timely release of delivery orders. Timely issuance of MRNs and WH invoices.


Accurate and timely CargoWise updates. Timely closure and reconciliation of jobs.


Customer satisfaction and response times.


Shipment processing accuracy.


Team productivity and compliance with procedures.


Achievement of departmental operational targets.




 


Qualifications and Skills:


 


Required Qualifications & Experience




Diploma or Bachelor's Degree in Logistics, Supply Chain Management, Business Administration, or a related field.


Minimum 3 years' experience in shipping, freight forwarding, logistics, or transportation operations.


Previous supervisory experience preferred.


Experience and working knowledge of CargoWise.


Sound understanding of customs clearance, shipping documentation, and freight forwarding procedures.




Skills & Competencies




Strong knowledge of shipping and freight forwarding processes.


Good understanding of customs and trade compliance requirements.


Ability to interpret Bills of Lading, manifests, delivery orders, invoices, and shipping documentation.


Strong leadership, communication, and organizational skills.


Customer-focused with strong problem-solving abilities.


Proficient in CargoWise and Microsoft Office applications.


Ability to work under pressure and meet deadlines.


High attention to detail and accuracy.

28718.description:
With more than 40 years of experience working in PNG, World Vision International Papua New Guinea (WVIPNG) focuses on helping the most vulnerable children and adults experience fullness of life.  Inspired by our Christian faith, WVPNG has an exciting opportunity for someone who may be looking for a change and wants to become part of a dynamic team helping vulnerable people and communities.


World Vision International Papua New Guinea (WVIPNG) has exciting opportunity for those of you who want a change and want to become part of a dynamic team. We are currently looking for suitable, qualified, experienced, and highly motivated professional to fill the role of 
Monitoring & Evaluation Officer
 to be based in 
Mt.Hagen, Western Highlands, Papua New Guinea.
 The position reports to the Monitoring and Evaluation Coordinator.


 


PURPOSE OF THE POSITION


The Monitoring and Evaluation Officer reports to the Monitoring and Evaluation Coordinator and supports implementation of the project’s monitoring, evaluation, accountability, and learning (MEAL) activities. Based in Western Highlands, the role collects, verifies, manages, and analyses project data; supports assessments, baselines, evaluations, and routine field monitoring; and prepares timely reports. The Officer works with project staff, partners, children, and communities to track results, strengthen data quality, implement community accountability processes, and document learning under the Coordinator’s guidance.


 


MAJOR ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES




Support the Coordinator to conduct project needs assessments, including gender equality, disability and social inclusion (GEDSI), climate, livelihoods, markets, and value chains, using approved tools.


Assist the Coordinator to implement the project MEAL framework, logframe, indicator tracking table (ITT), and MEAL workplan; maintain activity schedules and records.


Provide project data and field-level support for programme quality assignments requested by the Coordinator and Program Impact and Effectiveness Manager.


Assist in preparing, translating, and testing approved data collection tools for surveys, pre- and post-tests, post-implementation and post-distribution monitoring, focus group discussions, and key informant interviews.


Support baseline, midline, endline, and outcome monitoring studies by arranging field logistics, mobilising participants, and collecting data using approved methodologies and sampling plans.


Assist the Coordinator and evaluation consultants with field arrangements, document collation, data collection, and interpretation workshops for project baselines and evaluations.


Support training and day-to-day guidance of enumerators and casual data collectors; check completed forms, follow up missing information, and promptly raise field challenges with the Coordinator.


Assist project staff and partners with approved data collection, data entry, output monitoring, and reporting requirements through practical guidance and refresher sessions.


Update the project ITT each month, verify reported achievements against source documents, and submit accurate data and discrepancies to the Coordinator for review.


Conduct scheduled project site visits, spot checks, and data verification with staff and partners; document implementation progress, quality concerns, and follow-up actions.


Prepare monitoring findings for project reflection meetings and maintain an action tracker to follow up agreed recommendations with the Coordinator and project staff.


Compile monitoring summaries, indicator results, and supporting evidence for milestone and donor reports for review by the Coordinator and Project Team Leader.


Collect community views on preferred information-sharing and feedback channels, including the needs of children, women, and people with disabilities, to inform accountability activities.


Implement the approved community accountability plan by sharing accessible project information, supporting consultations, and encouraging meaningful participation.


Receive and securely record feedback and complaints, refer cases through approved channels, and track responses. Escalate safeguarding or sensitive concerns immediately and communicate authorised updates to communities.


Inform children and community members of their rights to information, consultation, participation, and safe feedback and complaints, using appropriate languages and accessible methods.


Support lessons learned events by organising field inputs, recording discussions, and documenting practical recommendations for project improvement.


Draft case studies and other knowledge products from verified project evidence, obtaining required consent and safeguarding clearance before use.


Maintain organised and secure paper and electronic records, protect personal information, and apply approved consent, confidentiality, and data protection procedures.


Attend relevant internal and external meetings as assigned by the Coordinator and share field updates and agreed follow-up actions.


Attend relevant training, workshops, and events, and perform other MEAL duties assigned by the Coordinator within the scope of the role.




EDUCATIONAL QUALIFICATION/SKILLS, KNOWLEDGE & EXPERIENCE




Degree in Mathematics, Statistics, International or Community Development, or a related field preferred.


Minimum two years of relevant monitoring and evaluation or data collection experience in a relief or development organisation.


Experience working with an international NGO is an advantage.


Practical experience supporting surveys, routine field monitoring, baselines, or evaluations using qualitative and quantitative methods.


Good organisational skills, attention to detail, and ability to support field data collection teams.


Ability to communicate clearly and respectfully with project staff, partners, children, and communities.


Working knowledge of MEAL processes, project indicators, logframes, and routine reporting requirements.


Good working knowledge of Microsoft Excel for data entry, cleaning, analysis, and preparation of tables and charts.


Willingness to work occasional overtime to meet reporting and fieldwork deadlines.


Flexibility to undertake additional relevant duties to support organisational objectives.


Strong data handling skills, including checking completeness and accuracy, coding, classification, and maintaining secure records.


Ability to interpret monitoring results and present clear findings in written summaries, tables, and charts.


Experience collecting and reporting sex-, age-, and disability-disaggregated data and monitoring inclusion outcomes is preferred.


Ability to work effectively in a team and complete assigned tasks with guidance from the Coordinator.


Ability to provide practical data collection guidance to staff and partners in a cross-cultural setting.


Fluency in English and Tok Pisin.


Willingness to travel to very remote communities and comply with World Vision’s safeguarding and field safety requirements.




A competitive salary, benefits, and career development opportunity will be offered commensurate with relevant experience, knowledge, and qualifications.


Interested applicants should submit the following documents all in 
one PDF file
 before;
 Wednesday 14 October 2026
, 
(Midnight, PNG Time).




Expression of interest


Detailed CV




World Vision is committed to the principles of workplace diversity. Qualified women and people with disabilities are encouraged to apply.


World Vision is committed to safeguarding all children and adults living where World Vision operates. We enforce a zero tolerance policy for any forms of violence, abuse and exploitation against children or adults, either by employees or others affiliated with our work. We do not employ staff whose background is not aligned with our safe guarding practices. Employment is conditional upon successful completion of all mandatory background checks, including criminal record checks, where required.


We appreciate the time it takes to prepare your application. Please note that only short-listed candidates suitable for interviews will be contacted. If you do not hear from World Vision within 
two (2) weeks
 of the closing date, please consider your application unsuccessful.


 


Applicant Type:


PNG Nationals Only.






Apply

28716.description:
With more than 40 years of experience working in PNG, World Vision International Papua New Guinea (WVIPNG) focuses on helping the most vulnerable children and adults experience fullness of life.  Inspired by our Christian faith, WVPNG has an exciting opportunity for someone who may be looking for a change and wants to become part of a dynamic team helping vulnerable people and communities.


World Vision International Papua New Guinea (WVIPNG) is seeking a suitably qualified, experienced and highly motivated professional to fill the role of Project Coordinator for The Sustainable Highlands Region Core Road Network Project (SHRCRNP), based in Mt. Hagen, Western Highlands, Papua New Guinea.


 


PURPOSE OF THE POSITION


The Project Coordinator coordinates planning, implementation, monitoring and reporting for SHRCRNP community climate resilience and livelihood activities. Based in Western Highlands, the role guides Project Officers and field teams, coordinates technical and partner inputs, monitors budgets and compliance, and oversees delivery of nature- and ecosystem-based solutions, climate-smart agriculture, community-based disaster risk reduction, market access and economic development initiatives. The Coordinator promotes inclusive participation, safeguarding and accountability, using project evidence and learning to improve delivery and achieve agreed results.


 


MAJOR ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES




Prepare consolidated implementation plans, schedules and delivery targets with Project Officers, field teams and technical specialists, aligned with the approved project design and budget.


Coordinate community needs assessments and planning for nature- and ecosystem-based solutions, climate-smart agriculture, disaster risk reduction, market access and economic development.


Coordinate government, partner and community engagement; clarify responsibilities, maintain delivery schedules and resolve operational issues within delegated authority.


Oversee implementation of climate mitigation and adaptation activities, ensuring technical standards, inclusive participation and agreed project approaches are applied.


Guide and supervise assigned Project Officers and field teams; review monthly workplans, organise field schedules and provide regular coaching and feedback.


Coordinate timely consultation with technical specialists on agriculture, ecosystem restoration, livelihoods, disaster risk and market access; escalate technical issues requiring specialist decisions.


Conduct regular field visits and review activity quality, progress, risks and delivery constraints with project staff and partners.


Work with the Monitoring and Evaluation Coordinator to align monitoring tools and reporting requirements, support field data collection and verify implementation records.


Review progress against workplans, outputs and expenditure; maintain action and risk trackers and recommend changes for authorised approval.


Coordinate field logistics, procurement requests and resource allocation with administration, procurement and finance teams, following approved procedures.


Promote gender equality, disability and social inclusion in implementation; monitor practical access barriers affecting women, youth and people with disabilities.


Coordinate operational support for assessments, baselines and evaluations with the MEAL team, including community engagement, field access and response to findings.


Monitor the activity budget and expenditure, review supporting documents and forecasts, and follow up variances with finance and the project manager.


Maintain grant, financial and operational compliance; apply procurement and approval limits and report suspected misuse or non-compliance through authorised channels.


Ensure staff and partners apply safeguarding, consent and confidentiality requirements; refer child or adult protection concerns immediately through designated channels.


Coordinate accessible information sharing, consultations and safe feedback channels with the MEAL team; monitor follow-up and share authorised responses with communities.


Consolidate and review monthly progress reports, assessment findings and milestone evidence; submit complete reports to the authorised manager within agreed deadlines.


Facilitate monthly learning and reflection sessions, present progress at relevant meetings and document lessons, case studies and agreed improvements with verified evidence and required consent.


Train and coach field staff on monthly work planning, documentation and reporting; identify capacity gaps and arrange relevant support.


Participate in relevant internal and external coordination meetings and follow up decisions with assigned staff and partners.


Attend relevant training and undertake other project coordination duties assigned by the supervisor within the scope of the role.




EDUCATIONAL QUALIFICATION/SKILLS, KNOWLEDGE & EXPERIENCE




Bachelor’s degree in Business, Project Management, or related field.


Diploma in Project Management or equivalent relevant project management training.


At least three years of project management experience in community development, relief or development programmes.


Experience coordinating project design, implementation, monitoring, evaluation and report writing.

28701.description:
Lead critical national energy infrastructure across multiple power sites
Senior role shaping safety, performance and operational strategy
Build strong teams and grow your career in PNG's energy sector
About Our Client
 Our client is a leading Papua New Guinean energy company that turns the nation's natural gas resources into reliable electricity for homes, businesses and industry. The company operates gas-fired generation assets across the country and supplies power into the national grid under long-term power purchase arrangements. It is helping to build PNG's energy security and its economic growth, and it is looking for a proven operations leader to join its Assets & Operations team.
 
The Opportunity
 This is a senior role leading the day-to-day operation of a modern open-cycle gas turbine power station in Central Province. Reporting to the Plant Manager, you will be responsible for plant reliability, availability and performance, with a strong focus on safety, environmental responsibility and cost efficiency. You will also support and oversee the company's other generation sites across PNG, so your influence will reach well beyond one plant.
 If you want real accountability for keeping the lights on, and a place to use your gas turbine expertise at a national scale, this role is for you.
 
Key Responsibilities
 
 
Lead the operational management of the power station, including its people, plant, equipment and facilities
 
Act as the company's main point of contact with key stakeholders
 
Contribute to the annual budget and operating plan, and produce monthly production and cost reports
 
Build, develop and retain capable operations and maintenance teams through targeted on-the-job training
 
Own, review and improve Standard Operating Procedures and Integrated Management System procedures
 
Lead periodic plant risk assessments and track availability, reliability and performance
 
Validate operator logs, daily performance reports and abnormality reports, and analyse alarms and operating trends
 
Review root cause and failure analysis investigations to make sure they are accurate and that lessons are shared
 
Act as Site Safety Leader, promoting a strong environmental, health and safety culture
 
Direct operations personnel through emergencies such as fire, security or environmental incidents
 
Ensure compliance with power purchase agreements, environmental permits and company policies
 
 
What You'll Bring
 
 
10+ years of plant management or O&M experience in power generation
 
Hands-on experience operating and maintaining gas turbines
 
A degree in Mechanical, Electrical or Instrumentation & Control Engineering, or an equivalent technical college qualification
 
Proficiency with SCADA, turbine fleet management software (e.g. Insight), Power Plant CMMS and MS Office
 
A strong track record of delivering high plant performance
 
Sound commercial awareness, including budget preparation and cost management
 
Excellent written and verbal communication in English
 
Exceptional leadership and organisational skills, and the ability to manage competing priorities under pressure
 
High integrity and discretion, a strategic and results-driven approach, and a commitment to building collaborative, inclusive teams
 
 
Ready to Take Charge?
 This is your chance to lead critical national infrastructure and help power Papua New Guinea's growth. If you are a safety-focused operations leader with deep gas turbine experience and a drive for operational excellence, we want to hear from you.
 
Click the "Apply Now" button on this advertisement to submit your application.
 
Peopleconnexion PNG: Recruitment, Training, Immigration, Payroll & HR Services.
www.peopleconnexion.com/png
Your legacy is our business

28585.description:
Newmont produces metals the world needs - safely, responsibly and with care for people, communities and the environment. With a 100+ year history, we continue to shape the future of mining through innovation and strong operational performance. By joining our inclusive, world-class team, you can help shape the future of mining and make a meaningful difference.


About Lihir


Lihir is one of the world's largest gold mining operations, located on Niolam Island in Papua New Guinea's New Ireland Province. The operation is renowned for its unique volcanic landscape and combines world-class mining and processing with a strong commitment to safety, sustainability, innovation and technical excellence.


The operation combines open-pit mining and gold processing in a remote island setting, supported by modern facilities and a culture focused on improving daily.


At Lihir, you'll be part of a team that is deeply connected to the island and the communities that call it home. We are committed to creating lasting benefits through local employment, training, scholarships and apprenticeship programs, while fostering a workplace where people look out for one another and succeed together.


With a culture grounded in safety, respect and delivering responsibly, Lihir offers the opportunity to develop your career while contributing to an operation that plays an important role in Papua New Guinea's economic and social development.


Purpose
The Services Technician will operate the assigned sections of the process plant (Grinding circuits, flotations, thickener operations, flotation reagent preparations and mill reline activities) so that all Safety & metallurgical targets are met on a shift-by-shift basis.


Essential Duties




Champion a strong safety culture by ensuring full compliance with all HSE policies and Fitness for Work standards. 


Perform tasks only when hazards and risks are clearly understood, working closely with Supervisors to confirm safe controls. 


Proactively monitor plant operations and implement strategies to minimise risks and maintain a safe working environment. 


Promptly report hazards, unsafe behaviours, and incidents in line with company standards. 


Collaborate effectively with diverse teams across departments to support operational success. 


Take ownership of your area, consistently delivering on commitments and maintaining high performance standards. 


Engage in ongoing development through training, shift handovers, toolbox talks, and team activities. 


Maintain high housekeeping standards within the process plant at all times. 


Operate plant equipment in line with daily plans and inspections, identifying and escalating defects or risks as required. 


Ensure all shift activities—including inspections, operational tasks, and SOP adherence—are completed safely and in full compliance with environmental and company guidelines.




Training & Experience




Prior experience in mineral processing


Tertiary qualification advantageous.


Certificates/Statements of Attainment in relevant metalliferous processing competencies highly regarded.


Minimum level of Grade 10 education desirable.


PNG driving License class 6 


Good verbal & written communication skills.


Self-motivated with the ability to work autonomously from time to time.


High attention to detail with good time management skills.


Strong active listening & interpersonal skills.




Working Conditions
This is a FIFO role on a 28/14 rotating roster.


At Newmont, our people are our strength and we’re committed to a safe, inclusive and supportive workplace. If you’re passionate about doing work that matters, join Newmont and help shape the future of mining.​


Learn more about our purpose and values: About Newmont​
Hear from our people: Life at Newmont​


Important: Newmont does not ask candidates to pay money or share sensitive personal data outside our secure application process. If this happens, please report it to our Business Integrity team:

Goodman Fielder Papua New Guinea is one of PNG’s largest food companies, manufacturing and distributing high quality Flour, Stock Feed, Snacks and Bakery products throughout the country. The company owns a host of iconic brands which include; Flame Flour, Flame Stockfeed, Bilas Bread, Arthur's Pie, Twisties, Skel Rice and the Meadow Lea range.


At GFI, we care about making everyday food better for everyone.


Our goal is to be the leading and most innovative food company with a mission to meet our customers’ needs for superior quality foods with brands that are trusted by families everywhere.  We are the go-to source of consumer, shopper, and customer insights to help our customer and business partners succeed.


We currently have an immediate vacancy for an 
Electrician
 to join our maintenance team
 in Lae.
 The elelctrician will be assigned to keep production and manufacturing equipment (s) running efficiently to meet the required production plans, at the Flour Mill plant. Responsible for shift coverage, handling the daily, weekly, and monthly maintenance tasks, which also involves troubleshooting Electrical/PLC/Automation/Process problems, and repair and maintain existing production equipment’s.


 


RESPONSIBILITIES:




Making Safety Work and Hygiene practises as a daily HABBIT at Workplace


Drive “Teamwork” practice in our working environment.


Execution of the Planned Maintenance Work Order Cycle Process (Preventative & Corrective Maintenance) – On time in Full


Required to monitor/Cover production lines as per overall production plans

Minimum Grade 12 High School Certificate


NCII, NCIII, Trade Certificate


Electrical License/ Tradesman Certificate




Technical Skills, (Motor Control, Basic PLC understanding, Electrical wiring under AS3000) 




Deep understanding with motor control --


Possess good electrical troubleshooting skills --


Able to work under pressure even in holidays or weekend. Responsible enough, --


Can understand basic principle of PLC




Experience (Technical and Behavioural)




Previous experience as Industrial Electrician in food manufacturing set-up


Ability to manage the job and meet the deadline


Responsible, Punctual and Reliable 


Possess honesty all the time


Minimum 3 years of experience, preferably in a manufacturing environment, with demonstrated success in a similar level position within the FMCG industries.
